BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.claim: The call to worship is followed by creation as proof that God deserves worship; the warning against partners follows because the creation evidence establishes that He has no partner in worship or creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.anchor: إلى آخره بوصف هو دليل استحقاقه للعبادة

AKHFASH:v1p60/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p60/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p60/r3.claim: كنتم أمواتا means you were dust and sperm, which count as dead; this is ordinary Arabic usage for a thing's former material or state.
AKHFASH:v1p60/r3.anchor: قوله {وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم} فانما يقول كنتم ترابا ونطفا فذلك [26ب] ميت

AKHFASH:v1p60/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p60/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p60/r4.claim: He illustrates the idiom with saying a garment was cotton, a date was unripe, or 'make this garment' while only yarn is at hand.
AKHFASH:v1p60/r4.anchor: تقول للثوب: "قد كان هذا قطنا" و "كان هذا الرطب بسرا"*

FARRA:v1p23/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p23/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p23/r5.claim: How can you disbelieve is an exclamation of astonishment and rebuke, not a plain question.
FARRA:v1p23/r5.anchor: على وجه التعجب والتوبيخ لا على الاستفهام المحض

FARRA:v1p23/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p23/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p23/r6.claim: The clause means “when you had been dead”; qad is understood because both states have already occurred, as in other past-state constructions.

NAHHAS:v1p204/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p204/r16.claim: كيف is an accusative noun built on fatḥa; its interrogative particle-like force would suggest sukūn, but yāʾ favors fatḥa.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r16.anchor: كيف اسم في موضع نصب وهي مبنية على الفتح وكان سبيلها أن تكون ساكنة

NAHHAS:v1p204/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p204/r17.claim: The reading estimates وقد كنتم أمواتا, with قد deleted; أمواتا is the predicate of كنتم.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r17.anchor: وكنتم أمواتا ) التقدير وقد كنتم أمواتا ثم حذفت قد ( أمواتا ) خبر كنتم

NAHHAS:v1p204/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p204/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p204/r18.claim: The suffixes in فأحياكم are accusative objects, as are the suffixes in ثم يميتكم and ثم يحييكم.
NAHHAS:v1p204/r18.anchor: فأحياكم ) الكاف والميم في موضع نصب بالفعل وكذا ( ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r3.claim: “How can you disbelieve?” is not a real question but a statement of reproach and reminder of God's blessings and power; grammatically kayfa is a circumstantial adverb modifying the disbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r3.anchor: لفظه الاستفهام وليس به، بل هو تقرير وتوبيخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r4.claim: The question may also convey astonishment at the strangeness of rejecting a benefactor; wāw in “while you were dead” marks a circumstantial clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r4.anchor: ومن قال إن كيف تقرير وتعجب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r5.claim: They say people were nonexistent before creation, were brought to earthly life, then underwent ordinary death and will be raised at the Resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r5.anchor: كنتم أمواتا معدومين قبل أن تخلقوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r6.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r6.claim: Another account begins with Adam as lifeless clay, then his enlivening by the spirit, followed by human death and resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r6.anchor: كنتم أمواتا بكون آدم من طين ميتا قبل أن يحيى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r7.claim: Qatāda interprets the first death as the descendants' existence in their fathers' loins before being brought into the world.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r8.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r8.claim: Another view says people were dead in the womb before ensoulment, then were brought to earthly life, died, and will be raised.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r8.anchor: كنتم أمواتا في الأرحام قبل نفخ الروح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says God brought forth human souls as particles, then caused them to die; He later gave them worldly life, followed by death and Resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r9.anchor: أخرج نسم بني آدم أمثال الذر ثم أماتهم بعد ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو صالح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r10.claim: They say people die the familiar death, are revived for questioning in the graves, die there, then are revived for the Resurrection.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r11.claim: A further report from Ibn ʿAbbās takes death as obscurity and lack of renown, then life as being honored and remembered through this religion and its Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p113/r11.anchor: كنتم أمواتا بالخمول فأحياكم بأن ذكرتم وشرفتم بهذا الدين

THALABI:v1p173/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p173/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p173/r8.claim: The address turns to Meccan polytheists: they were inert sperm in their fathers' loins, then alive in the womb and world, then die and are raised for return and recompense.
THALABI:v1p173/r8.anchor: أمواتا نطفا في أصلاب آبائكم فأحياكم في الأرحام

THALABI:v1p173/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p173/r9.speaker: يعقوب
THALABI:v1p173/r9.claim: He reads turjaʿun in the active form, making the addressees the agents of their return.
THALABI:v1p173/r9.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب: ترجعون، وبيانه بفتح الأول وكسر الجيم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r3.claim: “How” is an astonished question directed to disbelievers for believers to marvel at: God gave life to those once dust, will kill them in this world, resurrect them, and judge them as He wills.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:27-28/r4.claim: Since polytheists deemed resurrection extraordinary, God argued with them from His creation of the heavens and earth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r10.claim: أموات is a plural of both ميت and ميتة; its broken plural on أفعال is exceptional, since فعائل is expected for a word on فيعل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r10.anchor: أمواتا: جمع ميت، وهو أيضا جمع ميتة، وجمعهما على أفعال شذوذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r11.claim: كيف asks about a state but here carries reproach and affirmation; some also hear denial and amazement, since one capable of final judgment should not be denied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208/r11.anchor: كيف: قد تقدم أنه اسم استفهام عن حال، وصحبه معنى التقرير والتوبيخ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r1.claim: Some hear denial and amazement: one with such power and final control, who will reward and punish, should not be denied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: صحبه الإنكار والتعجب، أي إن من كان بهذه المثابة من القدرة الباهرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r2.claim: The hamza denies the act itself, while كيف denies its state; because an existing thing must have a state, denying the state entails denying the act, a stronger rhetorical move.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r2.anchor: والإنكار بالهمزة إنكار لذات الفعل، وبكيف إنكار لحاله وإنكار حاله إنكار لذاته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī formalizes the argument: denying any possible state of their unbelief proves that the unbelief itself cannot exist.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وتحريره أنه إذا أنكر أن يكون لكفرهم حال يوجد عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r4.claim: Direct address shifts from the prior third-person description and makes the rebuke stronger because it reaches the addressees directly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r4.anchor: وهذا الخطاب فيه التفات، لأن الكلام قبل كان بصورة الغيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r5.claim: The imperfect تكفرون rebukes persistent unbelief and avoids reproaching those who once disbelieved but later believed, as many Companions did.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r5.anchor: وأتى بصيغة تكفرون مضارعا ولم يأت به ماضيا وإن كان الكفر قد وقع منهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r6.claim: The wāw in وكنتم أمواتا is circumstantial; Abū Ḥayyān agrees with the majority that قد is understood before the past-tense clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r6.anchor: والواو في قوله: وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم: واو الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes the whole story through the return a circumstantial clause and answers that their knowledge of its beginning and end is the present state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p208#2/r7.anchor: لم تدخل الواو على كنتم أمواتا وحده، ولكن على جملة قوله: كنتم أمواتا إلى ترجعون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the need to make every clause circumstantial or posit present knowledge: the state can simply be that God created them by giving them life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r1.anchor: ولا يتعين أن تكون جميع الجمل مندرجة في الحال، إذ يحتمل أن يكون الحال قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r2.claim: The Prophetic saying to make a partner of God although He created you likewise treats God's creation as a reason one should not disbelieve.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r2.anchor: أن تجعل لله ندا وهو خلقك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r3.claim: Giving life after nonexistence combines the greatest gift of creation with continued care and provision, making unbelief especially incongruous; human nature recognizes God as sole creator.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r3.anchor: لأنه لا نعمة أعظم من نعمة الاختراع، ثم نعمة الاصطناع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r4.claim: On this reading, only you were dead and He gave you life is circumstantial; the clauses about later death, renewed life, and return are independent statements.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا الذي شرحناه يكون قوله تعالى: ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم ثم إليه ترجعون جملا أخبر الله تعالى بها مستأنفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r5.claim: Their first interpretation takes the first death as prior nonexistence, first life as creation, second death as ordinary death, and second life as resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r5.anchor: الموت الأول: العدم السابق قبل الخلق، والإحياء الأول: الخلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r6.claim: Their second interpretation begins with ordinary death, revival in the grave for questioning, and death again in the grave after questioning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210/r6.anchor: الموت الأول: المعهود في الدنيا، والإحياء الأول: هو في القبر للمسألة، والموت الثاني: في القبر بعد المسألة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r1.claim: They complete their second interpretation by identifying the second revival as resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r1.anchor: البعث، قاله ابن عباس وأبو صالح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r2.claim: Qatāda takes the first death as being in the fathers' loins, the first life as birth, then ordinary death and resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r2.anchor: أن الموت الأول: كونهم في أصلاب آبائهم، والإحياء الأول: الإخراج من بطون الأمهات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the first death was when Adam's descendants were extracted as particles; the first life is birth, then ordinary death and resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r3.anchor: أن الموت الأول: هو الذي اعتقب إخراجهم من صلب آدم نسما كالذر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r4.claim: Another view sees the first death in the man's semen entering the womb and remaining lifeless until the spirit is breathed; the second death and life are ordinary death and resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r4.anchor: أن الموت الأول: مفارقة نطفة الرجل إلى الرحم فهي ميتة إلى نفخ الروح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also interprets the first death as obscurity, the first life as honor and renown through Islam and the Prophet, then ordinary death and resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r5.anchor: أن الموت الأول هو الخمول، والإحياء الأول: الذكر والشرف بهذا الدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r6.claim: A seventh view says Adam began as clay, received spirit, and thereby gave life to his descendants, followed by ordinary death and resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r6.anchor: أن الموت الأول: كون آدم من طين، والإحياء الأول: نفخ الروح فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the first interpretation: unbelievers must admit the initial sequence, and once they concede creation, life, and death, denying resurrection becomes unsupported; Abū Ḥayyān calls this sound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r7.anchor: واختار ابن عطية القول الأول وقال: هو أولى الأقوال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r8.speaker: أهل الحقائق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r8.claim: Mystical readings interpret death and life as passing from shirk to monotheism, ignorance to knowledge, discord to harmony, or ego-life to the life of the heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r8.anchor: أحدها: أمواتا بالشرك فأحياكم بالتوحيد. الثاني: أمواتا بالجهل فأحياكم بالعلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r9.speaker: الشبلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r9.claim: Al-Shiblī interprets them as dead away from God and brought to life through Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r9.anchor: أمواتا عنه فأحياكم به، قاله الشبلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r10.speaker: ابن عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ reads the sequence as death to outward forms and life through unveiling inner realities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r10.anchor: أمواتا بالظواهر فأحياكم بمكاشفة السرائر، قاله ابن عطاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r11.speaker: فارس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r11.claim: Fāris reads it as dying to one's own witnessing, living by God's witnessing, then being stripped of one's signs and returned wholly to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p210#2/r11.anchor: أمواتا بشهودكم فأحياكم بمشاهدته ثم يميتكم عن شواهدكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the first death as being semen in the fathers' loins, then life, ordinary death, renewed life, and judgment; he also allows the second life to be in the grave or at resurrection, with return as resurrection or entry into recompense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r1.anchor: واختار الزمخشري: أن الموت الأول كونهم نطفا في أصلاب آبائهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's possible grave-life reading does not imply questioning or punishment in the grave, which his school denies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r2.anchor: لا يفهم منه أنه يحيا للمسألة في القبر، ولا لأن ينعم فيه أو يعذب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r3.speaker: أهل السنة والكرامية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r3.claim: Sunnis and Karrāmiyya affirm punishment in the grave; Sunnis say a dead unbeliever is revived for punishment and a sinner may be punished, while Karrāmiyya say the dead person is punished while dead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r3.anchor: وأهل السنة والكرامية أثبتوه بلا خلاف بينهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says abundant sound reports establish grave punishment, which must therefore be affirmed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r4.anchor: والأحاديث الصحيحة قد استفاضت بعذاب القبر، فوجب القول به واعتقاده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r5.speaker: صاحب المنتخب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r5.claim: The author of al-Muntakhab takes أمواتا as dust and semen, since Adam came from dust and his descendants, except Jesus, from semen; most regard applying dead to inanimate matter as figurative, while Qatāda transmits literal usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r5.anchor: واختار صاحب المنتخب أن المراد بقوله: أمواتا أي ترابا ونطفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects dust as the referent because it was never alive and so does not fit the state you were dead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r6.anchor: لا يظهر ذلك في التراب، لأن المخلوق من التراب لم يتصف بالصفة التي أنكرت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r7.claim: He prefers the period when people are established as semen in the womb through their developmental stages; the first life is the breathing of the spirit, then ordinary death and resurrection follow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r7.anchor: والذي نختاره أن كونهم أمواتا، من وقت استقرارهم نطفا في الأرحام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r8.claim: Calling existent inanimate matter dead is literal for those who allow that usage and a nearby metaphor for others; calling pure nonexistence dead is distant, unlike Qur'anic dead earth and Arabic أرض موات.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r8.anchor: وأما كونهم أمواتا، فمن ذهب إلى أن الجماد يوصف بالموت حقيقة فيكون إذ ذاك حقيقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r9.claim: The reading of the first death as obscurity and the first life as renown is a remote metaphor when literal or near senses are available.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p211/r9.anchor: وأما قول من ذهب إلى أن الموت الأول: هو الخمول، والإحياء الأول: هو التنويه والذكر، فمجاز بعيد هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r1.claim: He prefers the chronology that makes the first revival follow the first death immediately, preserving the sequential force of fa; other chronologies insert a long interval.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r1.anchor: وعلى ما اخترناه تكون الفاء دالة على معناها من التعقيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r2.speaker: قائل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r2.claim: One interpretation takes the first death as ordinary death and the first revival as resurrection for questioning, using the past tense for a certain future.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r2.anchor: ومن قال: إن الموت الأول: هو المعهود، والإحياء الأول هو للمسألة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r3.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r3.claim: Some infer that there is no punishment in the grave because the verse names two deaths and two lives, with no intervening life after worldly resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r3.anchor: وقد استدل بهذه الآية قوم على نفي عذاب القبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r4.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r4.claim: They reject the disbelievers’ statement about two deaths and lives as proof, since it is their speech and many affirm a pre-worldly life in Adam’s loins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r4.anchor: قالوا: ولا يجوز أن يستدل بقوله تعالى: ربنا أمتنا اثنتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r5.claim: Lack of mention of the questioning life does not establish its absence; alternatively, the second revival may be for questioning, followed by return to God after the resurrection life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r5.anchor: أنه لا يلزم من عدم ذكر هذه الحياة للمسألة عدمها قبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says two deaths describe most people, while some died three times, as in the man who passed a ruined town and Abraham’s birds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r6.anchor: قال الحسن: ذكر الموت مرتين هذا لأكثر الناس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r7.claim: The sequence of giving life, causing death, and reviving proves God’s exclusive power over these acts and establishes resurrection and gathering.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r7.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: فأحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم دليل على اختصاصه تعالى بذلك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r8.claim: The pronoun in “then to Him you return” refers to God; an omitted noun means return to His recompense, reward or punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r8.anchor: والظاهر في قوله تعالى: ثم إليه ترجعون أن الهاء عائدة على الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r9.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun as referring directly to recompense for deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r9.anchor: وقيل: عائدة على الجزاء على الأعمال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r10.claim: Another alternative takes it as the place where God will judge people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r10.anchor: وقيل: عائدة على الموضع الذي يتولى الله الحكم بينكم فيه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r11.claim: Another alternative refers the pronoun to the revival implied by “He gave you life,” explaining return as renewed helplessness like the beginning of life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r11.anchor:
وقيل:
عائدة على الإحياء المدلول عليه بقوله: فأحياكم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r12.claim: The corporealists use “to Him you return” to claim God occupies a place, but the wording gives them no proof.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p212/r12.anchor: واستدلت المجسمة بقوله: ثم إليه ترجعون، على أنه تعالى في مكان ولا حجة لهم في ذلك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r5.claim: The warning also tells covenant-breakers that God can revive them after death, gather them, and recompense their deeds, a severe threat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r5.anchor: والإعلام أن ناقضي عهده هو تعالى قادر على إحيائهم بعد الموت

BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r3.claim: After the invitation, examples, and responses to the evidence of divine oneness, the address turns sharply to rebuke those who persist in disbelief and to point toward release from loss through resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r3.anchor: صرف وجه الخطاب عن المواجهة من الحق تعالى وأجري على لسان لؤم وإنكار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r4.claim: The interrogative كيف exposes the absence of any excuse for continued disbelief; because it asks about perceptible states, it challenges them about the observable conditions in which they persist.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p78/r4.anchor: فجاء هذا الاستفهام لإيضاح انقطاع العذر في التمادي على الكفر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.claim: The phrase about being dead, then made alive, dying, and being revived can be attached to an implied command to remember these events; the beginning already lets the thoughtful infer the return.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.anchor: إذ من البدءة تعلم العودة لمن تدبر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.claim: Humanity was made for lasting life, not extinction: God created the cosmos for people, as provision, means, and support for their preservation and development.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.anchor: لم يخلق هذا النوع البشري للفناء بل للبقاء

DURR-FULL:v1p104/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r12.claim: People were once nothing, God created them, then they die and are resurrected on Judgment Day.
DURR-FULL:v1p104/r12.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة في قوله {وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم ثم يميتكم} قال: لم تكونوا شيئا فخلفكم

SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r1.claim: كيف asks about states, is built because it contains the interrogative hamza and on the lightest vowel, and rarely takes a preposition or acts as a conditional; it does not make a verb jussive, contra the Kufans.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r1.anchor: " كيف " اسم استفهام يسأل به عن الأحوال، وبني لتضمنه معنى الهمزة، وبني على أخف الحركات

SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r2.claim: If a noun substitutes for كيف or answers it while a following verb governs it, that noun is accusative; otherwise it is nominative. When the questioned noun follows, it is subject and كيف predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r2.anchor: وإذا أبدل منها اسم أو وقع جوابا لها فهو منصوب إن كان بعدها فعل متسلط عليها

SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r3.claim: كيف can occur with its verb omitted, as in 9:8, where the implied sense is كيف توالونهم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r3.anchor: وقد يحذف الفعل بعدها، قال تعالى: كيف وإن يظهروا عليكم [التوبة: 8] أي كيف توالونهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r4.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r4.claim: Sibawayh treats كيف here as accusative by resemblance to an adverbial; al-Akhfash instead parses it as a circumstantial accusative. Both make تكفرون its governor.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r4.anchor: " كيف " في هذه الآية منصوبة على التشبيه بالظرف عند سيبويه، أي: في أي حالة تكفرون

SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r5.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash parses كيف as a circumstantial accusative, meaning in what state you disbelieve; its subject is the pronoun in تكفرون.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r5.anchor: وعلى الحال عند الأخفش، أي: على أي حال تكفرون، والعامل فيها على القولين

SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa's gloss معاندين makes this a bare assertion of obstinate disbelief and loses the intended interrogative force of amazement, rebuke or denial.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r6.anchor: ثم قال: " والتقدير: معاندين تكفرون. وفي هذا التقدير نظر

SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the question as denial: since any existent must have some state, denying any state of disbelief denies its existence by proof.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري بعد أن جعل الاستفهام للإنكار: " وتحريره أنه إذا أنكر

SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r8.claim: The address shifts from third person about the disbelievers to direct address, making the rebuke more forceful.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r8.anchor: وفي الكلام التفات من الغيبة في قوله: " وأما الذين كفروا " إلى آخره، إلى الخطاب

SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r9.claim: The imperfect indicates persistence in disbelief, the object of censure, and avoids reproaching those who believed after earlier disbelief.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r9.anchor: وجاء " تكفرون " مضارعا لا ماضيا لأن المنكر الدوام على الكفر

SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r10.claim: كفر normally takes ب, as in the cited verses; it can take a direct object when it means جحدوا, as in Hud 11:68.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28/r10.anchor: و " كفر " يتعدى بحرف الجر نحو: { تكفرون بالله } تكفرون بآيات الله

SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r1.claim: The wāw is circumstantial, as shown by substituting إذ; the past clause is circumstantial and needs an implicit قد to license its past tense.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r1.anchor: الواو واو الحال، وعلامتها أن يصلح موضعها " إذ " ، وجملة { كنتم أمواتا } في محل نصب

SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the circumstantial scope includes the entire story: you were nonliving sperm in your fathers' loins, were made alive, then die, are raised and judged.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r2.anchor: كيف تكفرون بالله وقصتكم هذه وحالكم أنكم كنتم أمواتا نطفا في أصلاب آبائكم

SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r3.claim: To make past and future events a present circumstance, al-Zamakhshari says the present condition is knowing the whole story from beginning to end.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r3.anchor: قلت: هو العلم بالقصة كأنه قيل: كيف تكفرون وأنتم عالمون

SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r4.claim: The Sheikh calls al-Zamakhshari's account strained; the clauses after the first may be independent reports, distinguished by ثم and their verb form from the preceding clauses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ ما معناه: هذا تكلف، يعني تأويله هذه الجملة بالجملة الاسمية

SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r5.claim: The fāʾ marks immediate sequence and ثم delay: the first death is prior nonexistence, first life creation, second death ordinary death, and second life resurrection; return to recompense follows resurrection.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r5.anchor: والفاء في قوله: " فأحياكم " على بابها من التعقيب، و " ثم " على بابها من التراخي

SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن مسعود، مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r6.claim: The preferred mapping of the two deaths and two lives—nonexistence, creation, ordinary death and resurrection—is attributed to Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud and Mujahid.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r6.anchor: وهو أحسن الأقوال، ويعزى لابن عباس وابن مسعود ومجاهد، والرجوع إلى الجزاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r7.claim: The pronoun in إليه refers to God, as do the preceding pronouns; the omitted destination is His reward and punishment.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r7.anchor: والضمير في " إليه " لله تعالى، وهذا ظاهر لأنه كالضمائر قبله وثم مضاف محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r8.claim: Other proposed destinations for the return are recompense for deeds, the place where God adjudicates, or the earlier state of helplessness implied by your first creation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: على الجزاء على الأعمال. وقيل: على المكان الذي يتولى الله فيه الحكم بينكم

SAMIN-DURR:2:28#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#3/r1.claim: The majority read ترجعون passive; an active reading is also transmitted. رجع can be intransitive or transitive, so the passive fits its transitive use and the implied ثم يرجعكم, matching God's agency in earlier verbs while also suiting the verse endings.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#3/r1.anchor: والجمهور على قراءة " ترجعون " مبنيا للمفعول، وقرئ مبنيا للفاعل حيث جاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:28#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#3/r2.claim: أموات is the plural of ميت; though قياس would give a faʿāʾil plural like سيد/سيائد, the better analysis is plural of the lightened form ميت, like أقوال from قيل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:28#3/r2.anchor: وأموات جمع " ميت " وقياسه على فعائل كسيد وسيائد، والأولى أن يكون أموات جمع ميت مخففا

ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r1.claim: Their first lifeless state was as sperm, then they became living beings, died, were resurrected, and return to God after resurrection.
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r1.anchor: فكونهم أمواتا أولا أنهم كانوا نطفا ثم جعلوا حيوانا ثم أميتوا

ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r2.claim: The return is after resurrection; the cited descriptions say they hasten toward the caller and emerge swiftly from their graves.
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r2.anchor: كما قال (مهطعين إلى الداع) أي مسرعين. وقوله، عز وجل (يوم يخرجون من الأجداث سراعا). والأجداث القبور.

ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r3.claim: Kayfa is an interrogative expressing astonishment, addressed to people and believers: marvel that these people disbelieve despite God’s established proof.
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r3.anchor: وتأويل كيف أنها، استفهام في معنى التعجب

ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r4.claim: The phrase means ‘you had been’; the wāw is circumstantial, with qad understood from context.
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r4.anchor: ومعنى (وكنتم) وقد كنتم وهذه الواو للحال، وإضمار قد جائز

ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r5.claim: Qad may be omitted when the wording supplies evidence, as in the examples about constricted hearts and a shirt torn from behind.
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r5.anchor: وكذلك قوله (أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم) (وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر).

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r1.speaker: حمزة
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r1.claim: The word is read with imāla or tafkhīm; Hamza inclines comparable forms after wāw but not after fa, distinguishing connected from separate contexts by ease and heaviness.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ بالامالة والتفخيم على ما قدمنا القول في ذلك وانما ذكرت هذا الحرف لأن حمزة يميل أمثاله اذا كانت قبله الواو ولا يميله مع الفاء

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r2.claim: Because both forms have identical pronunciation, a treatment used for one should also be used for the other.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r2.anchor: واللفظ بهذين الحرفين واحد فمن استعمل وجها مع أحدهما لزمه استعماله مع الآخر أيضا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r1.claim: Wāw-root verbs prefixed with alif undergo imāla.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r1.anchor: وكل فعل من ذوات الواو زيد في أوله ألف فإنه يميله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r2.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī inclines these forms, including فأحياكم, and related wāw-root forms in al-Shams and al-Ḍuḥā.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r2.anchor: وكان الكسائي يميل ذلك كله ويميل ﴿ فأحياكم ﴾ و ﴿ أمات وأحيا ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir opens all the forms under discussion.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r1.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī applies the imāla whether wāw or fāʾ precedes the verb, or no particle precedes it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r1.anchor: وكان الكسائي يميل ذلك كله كان قبل الفعل واو أو فاء أو لم يكن قبله شيء مثل ﴿ أحياكم ﴾

QIRAAT-ER:2:28:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:28:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:28:16#1/r1.claim: The active Form I reading means you return and assigns people agency, unlike the standard passive you are returned.
QIRAAT-ER:2:28:16#1/r1.anchor: restores human agency to the act of returning, contrasting with standard passive

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r1.claim: The majority read turjaʿūn passively, from transitive rajaʿa; Abū Ḥayyān calls it more eloquent because God is subject of the preceding life-and-death verbs and the passive preserves the cadence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r1.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور أفصح، لأن الإسناد في الأفعال السابقة هو إلى الله تعالى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r2.speaker: مجاهد ويحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق وابن محيصن والفياض بن غزوان وسلام ويعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r2.claim: These readers use the active form, treating rajaʿa as intransitive; Abū Ḥayyān says it loses the semantic correspondence because someone may return without another person returning him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r2.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد، ويحيى بن يعمر، وابن أبي إسحاق، وابن محيصن، والفياض بن غزوان، وسلام، ويعقوب: مبنيا للفاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r3.claim: The passive preserves a semantic correspondence with the preceding divine acts and emphasizes God’s power and complete control over resurrection and return, though God is the agent of all things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r3.anchor: والمقصود هنا إظهار القدرة والتصرف التام بنسبة الإحياء والإماتة، والإحياء والرجوع إليه تعالى، وإن كنا نعلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r4.claim: The promise of return warns sinners and encourages the righteous by increasing fear of wrongdoing and hope for further good works.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r4.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: ثم إليه ترجعون من الترهيب والترغيب ما يزيد المسيء خشية ويرده عن بعض ما يرتكبه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r5.claim: The verse refutes materialists, deniers of God, and rejecters of resurrection by affirming that life, death, resurrection, and all affairs belong to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r5.anchor: وفيها رد على الدهرية والمعطلة ومنكري البعث، إذ هو بيده الإحياء والإماتة والبعث

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r1.claim: The address turns back to the earlier addressees after cataloguing their offenses; direct address rebukes more sharply than speaking of them in the third person, which might not reach them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r1.anchor: التفات إلى خطاب أولئك بعد أن عدد قبائحهم المستدعية لمزيد سخطه تعالى عليهم والإنكار إذا وجه إلى المخاطب كان أبلغ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r2.claim: Sibawayh treats كيف as an adverb and therefore always accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r2.anchor: اسم إما ظرف وعزى إلى سيبويه فمحلها نصب دائما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r3.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash does not treat كيف as an adverb: it is nominative with a subject and accusative with other predicates.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r3.anchor: أو غير ظرف وعزى إلى الأخفش فمحلها رفع مع المبتدأ ونصب مع غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r4.speaker: ابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r4.claim: Ibn Mālik says no one calls كيف an adverb because it denotes neither place nor time; Ibn Hishām approves calling it one metaphorically because it means “in what state.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r4.anchor: وادعى ابن مالك أن أحدا لم يقل بظرفيتها إذ ليست زمانا ولا مكانا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r5.claim: كيف is mostly interrogative and only rarely conditional; jussive use is unattested, though Kufans and Quṭrub allow it by analogy, and Ibn Mawhab’s claim that it can coordinate is dismissed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r5.anchor: وأكثر ما تستعمل استفهاما والشرط بها قليل والجزم غير مسموع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r6.claim: Here كيف combines a question with denial, astonishment, and rebuke, asking how they can disbelieve whether ignorant of God or aware of Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r6.anchor: وهي هنا للإستخبار منضما إليه الإنكار والتعجيب لكفرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r7.claim: If they know the account of their origin and end, they know a perfect Creator; acting despite this powerful deterrent is astonishing, and the wording charges them with obstinate disbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r7.anchor: وهو يستلزم العلم بصانع موصوف بصفات الكمال منزه عن النقصان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r8.claim: كيف intensifies the rebuke beyond a plain “you disbelieve”: denying any state that must accompany existence implies, by proof, denial of the disbeliever’s existence; it can also negate every conceivable state of disbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r8.anchor: التي لا تنفك ويلزم من نفيها نفى صاحبها بطريق البرهان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r9.claim: Divine questioning need not imply ignorance: a request for information may alert or rebuke the hearer; the interrogative can seek that understanding occur in someone who lacks it, without combining literal and figurative meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r9.anchor: لأنه إما أن يكون بمعنى طلب الخبر فلا نسلم المحالية إذ قد يكون لتنبيه المخاطب وتوبيخه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r10.claim: The author explains divine astonishment as directed toward the addressee or as expressing its intended effect; alternatively, it is handled according to the Salaf’s approach.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r10.anchor: وكذا لا استحالة في وقوع التعجيب منه تعالى بل قالوا إذا ورد التعجب من الله جل وعلا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r11.claim: The imperfect tense condemns continuing disbelief, not merely past disbelief, so the wording does not reproach those who later believed, such as most Companions.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p212/r11.anchor: وأتى سبحانه بتكفرون ولم يأت بالماضي وإن كان الكفر قد وقع منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r1.claim: The clause before ثم is a circumstantial clause attached to the subject of تكفرون, with قد necessarily understood; it means “how can you disbelieve when He created you?”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r1.anchor: بتقدير قد لا محالة خلافا لمن وهم فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r2.claim: Creation is a state that should prevent disbelief because human nature and reason are disposed to recognize that God alone creates.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r2.anchor: ولما كان مركوزا في الطباع ومخلوقا في العقول أن لا خالق إلا الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r3.claim: The clauses after the first may be resumptive rather than part of the circumstantial clause, since their conjunctions and forms differ; a stronger alternative treats the whole account as the state known to the addressees.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r3.anchor: والجمل بعد مستأنفة لا تعلق لها بالحال ولذا غايرت ما قبلها بالحرف والصيغة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r4.claim: Life is defined as a power arising from species-level equilibrium that gives rise to other powers; another definition is sensory capacity, though paralysis shows absent sensation can result from an impediment rather than absent life.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r4.anchor: والحياة قوة تتبع الإعتدال النوعي ويفيض منها سائر القوى وقيل القوة الحساسة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r5.claim: Those defining life by sensation likely mean touch: different senses belong to different organs, some animals lack particular senses, and identifying life with each would multiply or compose life in one individual.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r5.anchor: وكأنهم أرادوا من ذلك قوة اللمس لأن مغايرة الحياة لما عداه من الحواس ظاهرة فإنها مختصة بعضو دون عضو

ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r6.claim: Life is also used figuratively for growth and for human perfections such as intellect, knowledge, and faith; death is the opposite at each level, while divine life denotes God’s perfection in knowledge and power.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r6.anchor: وتطلق مجازا على القوة النامية لأنها من طلائعها ومقدماتها وعلى ما يخص الإنسان من الفضائل كالعقل والعلم والإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r7.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and Mujāhid takes the first death as prior nonexistence, the first life as creation, the second death as ordinary death, and the final life as resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r7.anchor: والمروي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود ومجاهد رضي الله تعالى عنهم أن المراد بالموت الأول العدم السابق والأحياء الأول الخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r8.claim: Some exacting scholars choose the prior-nonexistence reading, supported by “you were dead” and the final death’s attribution to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r8.anchor: واختاره بعض المحققين وادعى أن قوله تعالى ﴿ وكنتم أمواتا ﴾

ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r9.claim: Another view takes “dead” as the embryonic stages until ensoulment, the first life as breathing of the spirit after those stages, and the later death and resurrection in their ordinary senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p213/r9.anchor: واختار آخرون أن كونهم أمواتا هو من وقت استقرارهم نطفا في الأرحام إلى تمام الأطوار بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r1.speaker: الساليكوتي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r1.claim: Al-Sālikūtī’s explanation makes the embryonic bodies like the dead; whether this is figurative depends on defining death as loss of prior life, while absolute absence of life makes it literal, the common view.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r1.anchor: قاله الساليكوتي ويفهم كلام بعضهم أنه على معنى كالأموات على التفسير الثاني وإن فسر بعدم الحياة مطلقا كان حقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r2.claim: The most remote reading makes the first death ordinary death and the first life the grave’s questioning, using past tense for a certain future event.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r2.anchor: وأبعد الأقوال عندي حمل الموت الأول على المعهود بعد انقضاء الأجل والأحياء الأول على ما يكون للمسألة في القبر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r3.claim: This verse does not prove that grave punishment is absent: its silence about a life enabling such punishment is no evidence against it, and other proofs establish the matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r3.anchor: ثم لا دليل في الآية على المختار لنفي عذاب القبر إذ نهاية ما فيها عدم ذكر الأحياء المصحح له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r4.claim: The return to God does not prove that God occupies a place; it means assembly at the Resurrection, where He alone judges and command belongs to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r4.anchor: لأن المراد بالرجوع إليه الجمع في المحشر حيث لا يتولى الحكم سواه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r5.claim: The passive reading of ترجعون suits the verse-ending rhyme and the preceding sense; the author calls it more eloquent than the active reading of Yaʿqūb, Mujāhid, and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r5.anchor: على البناء للمفعول دون يرجعكم المناسب للسياق مراعاة للتناسب رءوس الآي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r6.claim: Although the disbelievers may doubt God’s role and not know future events, manifest rational and revealed signs make such knowledge available and remove their excuse.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r6.anchor: لأن تمكنهم من العلم لوضوح الأدلة آفاقية وأنفسية وسطوع أنوارها عقلية ونقلية منزل منزل العلم في إزاحة العذر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r7.claim: The audience may include believers as well as unbelievers: after proofs of monotheism and prophethood, warning and promise, the passage counts common and Israelite blessings; death is a blessing as a passage to eternal life and reunion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214/r7.anchor: أكد ذلك بأن عدد عليهم النعم العامة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ reads the stages inwardly: dead in outwardness, brought to life through unveiling of secrets, then dying to servitude’s traits and living through divine qualities.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.speaker: فارس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.claim: Fāris reads the stages as moving from the servants’ witnessing to God’s witnessing, then their own witnessing dies away until they return wholly to God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r1.claim: The rebuke asks how people can disbelieve after God has set out clear proofs and arguments.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r2.claim: They were lifeless sperm in their fathers' loins before God gave them life in the womb and in worldly life.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r3.claim: God causes them to die when their appointed lifespans end.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r4.claim: God raises them for resurrection, then returns them to Him in the afterlife to be recompensed for their deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r4.anchor: {ثم يحييكم} للبعث {ثم إليه ترجعون} أي تردون في الآخرة فيجزيكم بأعمالكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r5.speaker: يعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r5.claim: Yaqub reads this form throughout the Quran with open initial ya and ta, making it active voice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r5.anchor: قرأ يعقوب "ترجعون" في كل القرآن بفتح الياء والتاء على تسمية الفاعل.

BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r1.claim: Kayfa is an accusative circumstantial expression attached to the subject of disbelieving: how can you disbelieve while so situated?
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r1.anchor: {كيف تكفرون} كيف نصب حالا من الضمير في تكفرون

BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r2.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r2.claim: The question rebukes and marvels at actual disbelief despite inward and cosmic proofs; divine astonishment means prompting wonder, as Abū al-Layth explains.

BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r3.speaker: القاضي
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī offers an alternative: the question requests an account of the state in which they disbelieve.
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r3.anchor: وقال القاضي : هو استخبار والمعنى أخبروني على أي : حال تكفرون

BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r4.claim: Amwāt describes lifeless bodies: elements and food, then sperm and formed or unformed embryos.
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r4.anchor: أي : أجساما لا حياة لها عناصر وأغذية ونطفا ومضغا مخلقة وغير مخلقة

BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r5.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r5.claim: Al-Kashshāf questions calling inanimate matter dead, since mayt normally describes a form capable of life; Bursevī answers that the word can mean anything lacking life.
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r5.anchor: فإن قلت كيف قيل لهم أموات حال كونهم جمادا وإنما يقال ميت فيما تصح منه الحياة

BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r6.claim: God first gave life by creating and breathing spirits into people in their mothers' wombs; the fāʾ marks the sequence despite intervening stages.
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r6.anchor: بخلق الأرواح ونفخها فيكم في أرحام أمهاتكم ثم في دنياكم

BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r7.claim: At life's end God causes death; death demonstrates power and is a blessing because it leads to the everlasting second life.
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r7.anchor: عند انقضاء آجالكم وكون الأمانة من دلائل القدرة ظاهر وأما كونها من النعم

BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r8.claim: The second life is the grave's questioning: the dead hear departing footsteps and are asked about their Lord, Prophet, and religion; the delay marker rules out the resurrection life here.
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r8.anchor: للسؤال في القبور فيحيي حتى يسمع خفق نعالهم إذا ولوا مدبرين ويقال من ربك ومن نبيك

BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r9.speaker: التيسير
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r9.claim: Al-Taysīr takes the verse to affirm both punishment and comfort in the grave.
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r9.anchor: ودلت الآية على إثبات عذاب القبر وراحة القبر كما في "التيسير"

BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r10.claim: After resurrection all return to God alone for judgment, recompense, and being raised from their graves; disbelief despite this sequence is astonishing.
BURSEVI:v1p69#2/r10.anchor: بعد الحشر لا إلى غيره فيجازيكم بأعمالكم إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر

BURSEVI:v1p71/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71/r1.claim: Although people may claim not to know the resurrection and return, the signs God provided make them accountable as if they knew.
BURSEVI:v1p71/r1.anchor: تمكنهم من العلم بهما لما نصب لهم من الدلائل منزل منزلة علمهم

BURSEVI:v1p71/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71/r2.claim: God's ability to give life initially proves His ability to restore life, since beginning creation is no harder than repeating it.
BURSEVI:v1p71/r2.anchor: فإن بدأ الخلق ليس بأهون عليه من إعادته

BURSEVI:v1p72/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p72/r7.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya addresses believers with a call to oneness: they were atoms in Adam, then heard the primordial covenant and answered yes willingly.

BURSEVI:v1p72/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p72/r8.claim: In this reading, death is return to the fathers' loins and human nature, while the next life comes through the prophets and accepting their call.
BURSEVI:v1p72/r8.anchor: بالرجعة إلى أصلاب آبائكم وإلى عالم الطبيعة الإنسانية

BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r1.claim: The Najmiyya reading says the prophets guide people through tawḥīd and the path of sacred law toward the levels of Paradise before their return to God.
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r1.anchor: بدلالة الأنبياء وقدم التوحيد على جادة الشريعة إلى درجات الجنات

BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the address honors prophets and saints: they were concealed in nonexistence, then formed in the spirit world through divine care and love.
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r2.anchor: وإما خطاب تشريف للأنبياء والأولياء أي : أتكفرون وكنتم أمواتا في كتم العدم

BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r3.claim: For prophets and saints, death means leaving the witnessing of beauty for the grave of sense and imagination; they are revived respectively by revelation's light and faith's spirit.
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r3.anchor: ثم يميتكم بالمفارقة عن شهود الجمال إلى مقبرة الحس والخيال ثم يحييكم أما الأنبياء فبنور نور الوحي

BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r4.claim: The prophets return by ascension and saints by divine attraction, as in the command to return to the Lord.
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r4.anchor: أما الأنبياء فبالعروج وأما الأولياء فبالرجوع بجذبات الحق

BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r5.speaker: يعقوب
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r5.claim: Yaʿqūb reads turjaʿūn with an open tāʾ and kasra on the jīm, suggesting chosen return; the other readers' form signals return by compulsion.
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r5.anchor: إما بالاختيار كقراءة يعقوب ترجعون بفتح التاء وكسر الجيم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r1.claim: كيف is an interrogative of denial and amazement: denying any state in which their disbelief could occur is stronger than asking ‘Do you disbelieve?’ and fits the following circumstance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r1.anchor: تعجيب لكفرهم بإنكار الحال التي يقع عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r2.claim: After describing the disbelievers, the address turns directly to them and rebukes disbelief despite the circumstances that should have led them otherwise: ‘Tell me, in what state do you disbelieve?’
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r2.anchor: لما وصفهم بالكفر وسوء المقال وخبث الفعال

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r3.claim: They were lifeless bodies: elements and foods, mixtures and sperm, and embryos formed or not yet formed.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28/r4.claim: God gave them life by creating and breathing souls into them; فاء marks this as immediately connected with the preceding creation, unlike the later events.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r1.claim: God causes death when their appointed lifespans end.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r2.claim: The next life is resurrection at the trumpet’s blast, or life for questioning in the graves.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r2.anchor: بالنشور يوم ينفخ في الصور أو للسؤال في القبور

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r3.claim: Return is after resurrection for recompense, or being raised from graves for judgment; disbelief despite this history is astonishing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r3.anchor: أو تنشرون إليه من قبوركم للحساب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r4.claim: Though they may not yet know resurrection and return, the proofs provided make them effectively informed and remove their excuse; the first creation proves God can revive them again, since beginning creation is no harder than restoring it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r4.anchor: تمكنهم من العلم بهما لما نصب لهم من الدلائل منزل منزلة علمهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, the address includes both groups: after proofs of divine unity and prophethood and promises and threats, God recounts general and particular favors, making disbelief especially blameworthy because great favors magnify ingratitude.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r5.anchor: أو الخطاب مع القبيلين فإنه سبحانه وتعالى لما بين دلائل التوحيد والنبوة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r6.claim: Death counts as a favor because it leads to the second, true life, as stated in 29:64; the favor counted is the meaning of the entire story, not each clause separately, since some clauses are past and others future.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r6.anchor: لما كانت وصلة إلى الحياة الثانية التي هي الحياة الحقيقية

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, believers alone are addressed to remind them of favor and distance them from disbelief: once ignorant, they received knowledge and faith, then die, gain true life, and return to reward beyond human perception.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#2/r8.claim: Life properly means sensory power or what entails it; it is figuratively used for growth, as a precursor, and for human excellences such as reason, knowledge, and faith, as life’s perfection and end. Death is used analogously for each opposite.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r1.claim: The cited verses use life and death across bodily, earthly, and spiritual senses: God gives life and death, revives the earth, and revives one who was dead by giving him light.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r2.claim: When life is predicated of God, it means that He can be characterized by the knowledge and power associated with life in creatures, or a real attribute of His essence that entails these qualities metaphorically.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r2.anchor: وإذا وصف به الباري تعالى أريد بها صحة اتصافه بالعلم والقدرة اللازمة لهذه القوة فينا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r3.speaker: يعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r3.claim: Yaʿqūb reads ترجعون with fatḥa on the tāʾ throughout the Qur’an.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:28#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب ترجعون بفتح التاء في جميع القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r1.claim: The cited challenge that the Creator of heaven and earth can create their likeness supports the claim that God can raise the dead.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r1.anchor: أو ليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r2.claim: Death and life are paired and dependent: if a second death had no following life, it would be extinction rather than death in its proper sense.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r2.anchor: الموت والحياة مزدوجان متضايفان , وإذا استوفى الموت الأول إحياؤه فلا بد من استيفاء الموت الثاني إحياؤه أيضا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r3.claim: Death is a transient hidden beginning before manifestation, while life is an enduring, established end; mortality passes and life remains.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r3.anchor: حقيقة الموت حال غيب بين يديه ظهور , والحياة نهاية ثابتة , والموت مبدأ غيب زائل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r4.claim: Biqai cites as sound a Prophetic report that death will be slaughtered, signaling the end of death as a kind and the permanence of life.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r4.anchor: ورد ما صح عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام في أن الموت يذبح , إعلام بانقضاء جنسه وثبات الحياة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r5.claim: The wording in 67:2 mentions death before life because the definite article encompasses both kinds, with life following death in the wording.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r5.anchor: ولذلك قدم في الذكر وأعقب بالحياة حيث استغرقتهما كلمة ( أل ) في قوله :

BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r6.claim: Biqai cites the Prophet’s statement that the bliss of Paradise has no end; no grading is stated for this report.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r6.anchor: كما ورد عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله : ( نعيم الجنة لا آخر له )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r7.claim: The second revival raises people after burial and the barzakh, restoring their former capacity to move by the power that first created and caused them to die.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r7.anchor: فينشركم بعد طيكم ويبعثكم بعد حبسكم في البرزخ ,

BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r8.claim: The account of resurrection does not rule out that people have some awareness in the barzakh before receiving their complete bodily form.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r8.anchor: وهذا لا ينفي أن يكون لهم في البرزخ إحساس بدون هذه الهيئة الكاملة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r9.claim: The return is a gathering after a long standing for recompense through reward or punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r9.anchor: فيحشركم بعد طول الوقوف للجزاء من الثواب والعقاب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r10.claim: Al-Harali says those who do not return voluntarily through worldly knowledge will be compelled after resurrection, when their supposed helpers and objects of worship fail them, and then judged.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p80/r10.anchor: كما قال الحرالي : إعلام بأنهم إن لم يرجعوا إلى الله سبحانه بداعي العلم في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r1.claim: Biqai identifies 2:281 as the last verse revealed: it is the final address encompassing all who face judgment, with no later comprehensive statement beyond it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r1.anchor: وهذا آخر خطاب الإقبال عليهم من دعوة الله لهم ولسان النكير عليهم , ولذلك كانت آية :

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r2.claim: Return means that a thing comes back to its point of origin when it reaches the end of its course.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r2.anchor: والرجع عود الشيء عند انتهاء غايته إلى مبدئها

DURR-FULL:v1p105/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r1.claim: An unattributed transmitted gloss says people were nothing in their fathers' loins, then created, truly killed, and truly raised at resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r1.anchor: في قوله {وكنتم أمواتا} في أصلاب آبائكم لم تكونوا شيئا حتى خلقكم

DURR-FULL:v1p105/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r2.claim: Qatada says people were dead in their fathers' loins, brought forth alive, then underwent inevitable death and resurrection: two lives and two deaths.
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: كانوا أمواتا في أصلاب آبائهم فأحياهم الله فأخرجهم ثم أماتهم الموتة التي لابد منها ثم أحياهم

DURR-FULL:v1p105/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r3.claim: Abu Salih places the revival in the grave, followed by another death.
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r3.anchor: عن أبي صالح في الآية قال {يميتكم ثم يحييكم} في القبر ثم يميتكم

DURR-FULL:v1p105/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r4.claim: Mujahid explains that people were nothing until created, then die and are raised; he connects this sequence to 40:11.
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في الآية قال: لم تكونوا شيئا حتى خلقكم ثم يميتكم موتة الحق ثم يحييكم وقوله (ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين) مثلها

DURR-FULL:v1p105/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya says they were nothing, then died and were revived, and after resurrection return to God following that life.
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية في الآية يقول: لم يكونوا شيئا ثم أماتهم ثم أحياهم ثم يوم القيامة يرجعون إليه بعد الحياة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r1.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the two deaths and two lives mentioned in 40:11 with the sequence described here.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r1.anchor: عن أبي الاحوص عن عبد الله : قالوا ربنا امتنا اثنتين واحييتنا اثنتين : قال : هي التي في البقرة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r2.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account, the first death is being dust before creation, life is creation, the second death is return to the graves, and the second life is resurrection.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس في قوله : ربنا امتنا اثنتين واحييتنا اثنتين قال كنتم ترابا قبل ان يخلقكم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r3.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas places the initial lifeless state in the fathers' loins; creation gives life, then comes actual death and resurrection. Abu al-Aliya, Hasan, Abu Salih, al-Suddi, and Qatadah are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r3.anchor: عن عطاء عن ابن عباس : كنتم امواتا فاحياكم في اصلاب ابائكم لم تكونوا شيئا حتى خلقكم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains that people return to God after life.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p73/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية : ثم اليه ترجعون قال : ترجعون اليه بعد الحياة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r1.claim: The circumstantial clause answers how disbelief is possible and offers the first proof of God’s existence and power: each person knows they came into being after nonexistence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r1.anchor: جملة حالية وهي تخلص إلى بيان ما دلت عليه ( كيف ) بطريق الإجمال وبيان أولى الدلائل على وجوده وقدرته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r2.claim: Human life emerges through a wondrous sequence: lifeless elements enter food, bodily constituents and gametes, then clot and morsel, before the spirit is breathed and life begins; this should establish God’s exclusive divinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r2.anchor: ثم امتزج فصار علقة ثم مضغة كل هذه أطوار أولية لوجود الإنسان وهي موجودات ميتة ثم بثت فيه الحياة بنفخ الروح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r3.claim: If death means absence of life in a body capable of life, the developing embryo can commonly be called dead before acquiring life; this prepares the sequence of enlivening, death, and resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r3.anchor: وإطلاق الأموات هنا مجاز شائع بناء على أن الموت هو عدم اتصاف الجسم بالحياة سواء كان متصفا بها من قبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r4.speaker: أئمة اللغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r4.claim: Many leading lexicographers, followed by al-Zamakhshari and al-Sakkaki, define death as loss of life after life existed; on this apparent sense, the pre-life “dead” is metaphorical, though Qur’anic usage is familiar either way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p375#2/r4.anchor: وقال كثير من أئمة اللغة الموت انعدام الحياة بعد وجودها وهو مختار الزمخشري والسكاكي وهو الظاهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r1.claim: In religious usage life is the spirit’s infusion into a body; philosophers have not given a strict definition, but descriptively it is a power producing sensation and motion under a suitable bodily temperament.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r1.anchor: والحياة ضد الموت ، وهي في نظر الشرع نفخ الروح في الجسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r2.claim: Life begins when the body’s balanced composition and vital spirit yield an appropriate temperament; it persists while that order holds and ceases when it breaks down.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r2.anchor: فباعتدال ذلك التركيب يكون النوع معتدلا ولكل صنف من ذلك النوع مزاج يخصه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r3.claim: A Tirmidhi report from Ibn Masʿud, quoting the Prophet, describes forty days as a drop, then equivalent periods as clot and morsel, after which an angel breathes in the spirit; Ibn Ashur gives no grading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r3.anchor: حديث الترمذي عن عبد الله بن مسعود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r4.claim: Death is nonexistence and life a positive state, and both are created by God, as affirmed in 67:2.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r4.anchor: فالموت عدم والحياة ملكة وكلاهما موجود مخلوق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r5.claim: The verse’s purpose is proof, not a statement of blessings: it juxtaposes life, which people count as a favor, with the two deaths they do not count as favors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p376/r5.anchor: الامتنان بل هو استدلال محض ذكر شيئا يعده الناس نعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r1.claim: The resurrection clause either teaches a conclusion rather than proving it to deniers, or follows from the justice and wisdom of a Creator who would not leave good and evil deeds unrewarded in this life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r1.anchor: فذلك تفريع عن الاستدلال وليس هو بدليل إذ المشركون ينكرون الحياة الآخرة فهو إدماج وتعليم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r2.claim: Return to God is pictured as a traveler’s return home: creation began from God, and resurrection brings people back for judgment and recompense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r2.anchor: شبه الحضور للحساب برجوع السائر إلى منزله باعتبار أن الله خلق الخلق فكأنهم صدروا من حضرته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r3.claim: Preposing إليه creates true restriction, informing deniers that return is to God alone and that their idols cannot help them at resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r3.anchor: وتقديم المتعلق على عامله مفيد القصر وهو قصر حقيقي سيق للمخاطبين لإفادتهم ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r4.claim: Most readers use the passive, depicting God returning people despite their denial; Yaʿqub reads the verb actively, describing their return without specifying whether it is voluntary or compelled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p377/r4.anchor: و { ترجعون } بضم التاء وفتح الجيم في قراءة الجمهور ، وقرأه يعقوب بفتح التاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r1.claim: The first of the previously discussed explanations is preferable: acknowledging prior nonexistence, worldly life, and then death leaves unbelievers no escape from acknowledging the final resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد رحمه الله: والقول الأول هو أولى هذه الأقوال، لأنه الذي لا محيد للكفار عن الإقرار به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r2.claim: Attributing their initial dead state to themselves as nonexistence, then attributing death to God, strengthens the argument; denial of the later resurrection is unsupported.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r2.anchor: ثم إن قوله أولا كنتم أمواتا وإسناده آخرا الإماتة إليه تبارك وتعالى مما يقوي ذلك القول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r3.claim: The pronoun in “to Him” refers to God, meaning return to His reward or punishment; the alternative refers it to resurrection, but the first is clearer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r3.anchor: والضمير في إليه عائد على الله تعالى أي إلى ثوابه أو عقابه، وقيل هو عائد على الإحياء، والأول أظهر.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r4.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r4.claim: Most readers pronounce turjaʿūn with tāʾ ḍamma and jīm fatḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r4.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «ترجعون» بضم التاء وفتح الجيم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r5.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Yaʿmar, Salam, Fayyad ibn Ghazwan, and Yaʿqub al-Hadrami read the forms with fatḥa on initial yāʾ or tāʾ wherever they occur.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق وابن محيصن وابن يعمر وسلام والفياض بن غزوان ويعقوب الحضرمي: «يرجع ويرجعون وترجعون»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r1.claim: They read kayfa as an expression of wonder, inviting believers to marvel that these people disbelieve despite God’s proof against them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه استفهام في معنى التعجب وهذا التعجب للمؤمنين أي اعجبوا من هؤلاء كيف يكفرون وقد ثبتت حجة الله عليهم قاله ابن قتيبة والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r2.claim: The question is a forceful affirmation and rebuke (‘Woe to you, how can you disbelieve?’); al-ʿAjjāj’s line uses a question to assert that an old man is not dancing in delight.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه استفهام خارج مخرج التقرير والتوبيخ تقديره ويحكم كيف تكفرون بالله قال العجاج أطربا وأنت قنسري والدهر بالانسان دواري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ supplies an implied qad: ‘you had indeed been lifeless’; he cites the same ellipsis in 4:90 and 12:26.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r3.anchor: قال الفراء أي وقد كنتم أمواتا ومثله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل والفراء وثعلب والزجاج وابن قتيبة وابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r4.claim: The soundest account is that the first lifeless state was as sperm, clots, and morsels; God gave life in the womb, causes worldly death, then resurrects for Judgment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p57/r4.anchor: أصَحها أن الموتة الأولى كونهم نطفا وعلقا ومضغا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r1.claim: God argues from His existence, power, and control: people should not deny Him or worship another, since He brought them from nonexistence into being.
