IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى محتجا على وجوده وقدرته، وأنه الخالق المتصرف في عباده:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r2.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the two deaths and two lives in Ghafir 11 with this verse's sequence of nonexistence, life, death, and renewed life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r2.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري، عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي الأحوص، عن عبد الله بن مسعود، رضي الله عنه:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r3.claim: Through ʿAta, Ibn Abbas explains the first death as nonexistence in the fathers' loins, followed by creation, true death, and resurrection; he equates this with Ghafir 11.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r4.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, counts dust before creation as the first death, creation as life, burial as the second death, and resurrection as the second life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} قال: كنتم ترابا قبل أن يخلقكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r5.speaker: السدي وابن مسعود وابن عباس وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r5.claim: Al-Suddi's transmission from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, and Companions, along with reports from Abu al-ʿAliya, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatada, and others, gives the same basic explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r5.anchor: وهكذا روي عن السدي بسنده، عن أبي مالك وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس -وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r6.speaker: أبو صالح عن السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r6.claim: A report from Abu Salih through al-Suddi says that God revives people in the grave and then causes them to die.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r6.anchor: وقال الثوري، عن السدي عن أبي صالح: {كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says God created humanity in Adam's back, took their covenant, caused them to die, created them in wombs, caused another death, and will resurrect them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p212/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جرير عن يونس، عن ابن وهب، عن عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم؛ خلقهم في (6) ظهر آدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the Ibn Zayd report and the preceding grave-life report unusual, and prefers the explanation from Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and the Tabiʿun; he links it to Ghafir 26.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r1.anchor: وهذا غريب والذي قبله. والصحيح ما تقدم عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس، وأولئك الجماعة من التابعين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r2.claim: Calling the preexistent state “dead” compares its lack of perception with idols called dead and the dead earth brought to life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r2.anchor: [وعبر عن الحال قبل الوجود بالموت بجامع ما يشتركان فيه من عدم الإحساس، كما قال في الأصنام: {أموات غير أحياء}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r3.claim: The verse's sequence is parallel to God's statement that He gives life, causes death, and gathers people for the Day of Resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213/r3.anchor: وهو كقوله تعالى: {قل الله يحييكم ثم يميتكم ثم يجمعكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون}

JISHUMI:v1p302/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r4.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v1p302/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the relevant yāʾ and tāʾ forms with fatḥa as active verbs throughout the Qur’an; other readers use passive forms, with exceptions.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r4.anchor: قرأ يعقوب في الياء والتاء بفتحها على أن الفعل لهم في جميع القرآن

JISHUMI:v1p302/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p302/r5.claim: Death is the opposite of life, and the two alternate in living beings.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r5.anchor: الموت ضد الحياة، وهما يتعاقبان على الجملة

JISHUMI:v1p302/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p302/r6.claim: Life is an accident by which humans and other animals live, and only God can bring it about.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r6.anchor: ولا خلاف أن الحياة عرض يحيا به الإنسان وسائر الحيوانات، ولا يقدر عليه إلا الله

JISHUMI:v1p302/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r7.speaker: الأكثر
JISHUMI:v1p302/r7.claim: Most hold that death is an accident opposed to life, citing God’s creation of death and life.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r7.anchor: فالأكثر على أنه عرض يضاد الحياة؛ ولذلك قال: (خلق الموت والحياة)

JISHUMI:v1p302/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r8.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v1p302/r8.claim: Abū Hāshim is reported to hold that death is not a positive entity or accident.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r8.anchor: وقيل: ليس بمعنى، عن أبي هاشم

JISHUMI:v1p302/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p302/r9.claim: To return to something means to go back to it.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r9.anchor: والرجوع في الشيء: هو العود إليه

JISHUMI:v1p302/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p302/r10.claim: Kayfa asks about a state and ranges over all states, just as kam ranges over numbers, mā over kinds, ayna over places, and man over rational beings.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r10.anchor: و(كيف) ينتظم جميع الأحوال، كما أن (كم) ينتظم جميع الأعداد

JISHUMI:v1p302/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p302/r11.claim: Kāna governs a nominative subject and accusative predicate; it has complete, incomplete, extra, and implicit-subject uses.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r11.anchor: وعمله أن يرفع الاسم وينصب الخبر، تقول: كان زيد قائما

JISHUMI:v1p302/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p302/r12.claim: Kāna is conjugated like a verb but is not truly a verb: it indicates time and enters a nominal subject-predicate construction.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r12.anchor: فليس بفعل على الحقيقة وإنما يدل على الزمان، ويدخل على الابتداء والخبر

JISHUMI:v1p302/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p302/r13.claim: Kāna has complete, incomplete, extra, and implicit-subject uses.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r13.anchor: و (كان) على أربعة أوجه: تامة، وناقصة، وزائدة، ومضمنة

JISHUMI:v1p302/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p302/r14.claim: In its extra use, kāna adds emphasis while its entry can be removed without changing the sentence’s basic meaning.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r14.anchor: والزائدة: ما يكون دخولها كخروجها إلا بمقدار ما توجبه من التوكيد

JISHUMI:v1p302/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p302/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p302/r15.claim: He illustrates extra kāna with 19:29, explaining the statement as asking how they could speak to a child in the cradle.
JISHUMI:v1p302/r15.anchor: أي كيف نكلم من في المهد صبيا

JISHUMI:v1p305/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r1.claim: The second life refers to the grave and its punishment; reading it as life in Paradise would make the following return to God incoherent.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r1.anchor: على الحياة في الجنة لم يستقم قوله: ثم إليه ترجعون؛ لأن تلك الحياة

JISHUMI:v1p305/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r2.claim: The statement that people return to God establishes resurrection.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r2.anchor: ويدل قوله ثم إليه ترجعون على إثبات المعاد

JISHUMI:v1p305/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r3.claim: God bestowed blessings on unbelievers, contrary to the Mujbira claim that He grants them no favor.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r3.anchor: وتدل الآية على أنه تعالى أنعم على الكفار؛ لذلك عد عليهم ما عد بخلاف قول المجبرة

JISHUMI:v1p305/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r4.claim: Worldly benefits still count as favors even if the unbeliever is destined for the Fire; they are like a poisoned dish and are diminished by grave wrongdoing.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r4.anchor: ولا يحمل على نعم الدنيا؛ لأنه إذا كان خلقه للنار لم يعتد بنعم الدنيا

JISHUMI:v1p305/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r5.claim: God’s power to give life a second time follows from His power to give it the first time.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r5.anchor: وتدل على أنه قادر على الإحياء الثاني من حيث قدر على الإحياء الأول

JISHUMI:v1p305/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r6.claim: Greater benefaction makes disobedience to the benefactor more serious; hence the rebuke, How can you disbelieve?
JISHUMI:v1p305/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن عظم النعمة يوجب عظم معصية المنعم، لذلك قال: كيف تكفرون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r1.claim: The question means ‘do you disbelieve?’ and expresses reproach and astonishment because their circumstances call them to faith and divert them from disbelief.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r1.anchor: مثله في قولك أتكفرون بالله ومعكم ما يصرف عن الكفر ويدعو إلى الإيمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r2.claim: Though disbelief is possible, the question casts it as impossible because the reasons leading them to faith are so strong.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r2.anchor: قلت قد اخرج في صورة المستحيل لما قوى من الصارف عن الكفر والداعي إلى الإيمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r3.claim: How denies the state in which they disbelieve; since a state depends on its subject’s existence, denying every possible state indirectly denies disbelief itself, a forceful argument.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#2/r3.anchor: كان إنكارا لوجوده على الطريق البرهاني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r1.claim: The wāw introduces a circumstantial clause; it attaches to the whole account through ‘you will return,’ not just the past clause.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r2.claim: They were lifeless sperm in their fathers’ loins; God gave them life, will cause them to die, revive them, and then reckon with them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r2.anchor: كأنه قيل كيف تكفرون بالله وقصتكم هذه وحالكم أنكم كنتم أمواتا نطفا في أصلاب آبائكم فجعلكم احياء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r3.claim: Although the account spans past and future, the present circumstance is their knowledge of the whole story, from its beginning to its end.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p150#3/r3.anchor: هو العلم بالقصة كانه قيل كيف تكفرون وأنتم عالمون بهذه القصة باولها وآخرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r1.claim: The question rejects their state and thereby their disbelief itself: their astonishing disbelief persists despite awareness of their condition.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r1.anchor: وأن إنكار الحال متضمن لإنكار الذات على سبيل الكناية فكأنه قيل ما أعجب كفركم مع علمكم بحالكم هذه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r2.claim: Even if they did not directly know of the second revival and return, arguments could establish them so firmly that this counts as knowledge; many knew yet persisted defiantly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r2.anchor: قد تمكنوا من العلم بهما بالدلائل الموصلة اليه فكان ذلك بمنزلة حصول العلم وكثير منهم علموا ثم عاندوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r3.claim: أموات is the plural of ميت, following the pattern of أقوال as the plural of قيل.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r3.anchor: والأموات جمع ميت كالأقوال في جمع قيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r4.claim: Calling inert matter dead is valid because dead can describe anything lacking life; the Qur’an uses this for a town and the earth.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r5.claim: Alternatively, ‘dead’ is metaphorical because inert matter and the dead share an absence of spirit and sensation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r5.anchor: ويجوز ان يكون استعارة لاجتماعهما في ان لا روح ولا إحساس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r6.claim: One interpretation takes the second life as life in the grave and the return as resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r6.anchor: قلت ما المراد بالإحياء الثاني قلت يجوز ان يراد به الإحياء في القبر وبالرجوع النشور

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r7.claim: Alternatively, the second life is resurrection and the return is arrival at recompense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r7.anchor: وأن يراد به النشور وبالرجوع المصير إلى الجزاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r8.claim: The first fāʾ indicates immediate succession from death to first life, while then marks the delays before death, revival, and final recompense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r8.anchor: لأن الإحياء الأول قد تعقب الموت بغير تراخ واما الموت فقد تراخى عن الإحياء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r9.claim: Their story supplies both clear signs that should turn them from disbelief and immense blessings that should prompt gratitude.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r9.anchor: يحتمل الأمرين جميعا لأن ما عدده آيات وهي مع كونها آيات من اعظم النعم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r1.claim: The question may be a rebuke of those who disbelieve.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, it expresses astonishment: “Marvel at them—how do they disbelieve?”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r2.anchor: أنه خارج مخرج التعجب , وتقديره : اعجبوا لهم , كيف يكفرون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd say people were nothing, were created, die at the end of their terms, and are raised on Judgment Day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r3.anchor: يوم القيامة , وهذا قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r4.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reads the first death as being in the graves, followed by life for questioning, death again, then resurrection at the trumpet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r4.anchor: عند نفخ الصور للنشور , لأن حقيقة الموت ما كان عن حياة , وهذا قول أبي صالح

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r5.claim: Qatāda takes the first state as being in the fathers’ loins, then birth, ordinary death, and resurrection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r5.anchor: للبعث يوم القيامة , وهذا قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd begins with the covenant: God gave Adam’s descendants life and reason in his loins to take their pledge, then they died; gestation, birth, worldly death, and resurrection follow. He links this to 39:6.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r6.anchor: بالنشور للبعث يوم القيامة , [ وهذا ] قول ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r7.claim: Another account counts two deaths and two lives: the sperm leaves the man, receives spirit and becomes human, dies, then is raised.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r7.anchor: فهو ميت إلى يوم ينفخ في الصور , فيرد في جسده روحه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r8.claim: A sixth view calls people forgotten and without trace, then “alive” when they become known; its proponent cites Abū Bujayla al-Saʿdī.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p90#2/r8.anchor: واستشهد من قال هذا التأويل بقول أبي بجيلة السعدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92/r1.claim: One reading takes the return as reaching the place where God will judge between you.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92/r1.anchor: إلى الموضع الذي يتولى الله الحكم بينكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92/r2.claim: The other reading takes it as return for recompense according to deeds.

MUQATIL:2:28-29/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r1.claim: The question challenges how people can disbelieve in God when He is one, without a partner.
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r1.anchor: { كيف تكفرون بالله } بأنه واحد لا شريك له،

MUQATIL:2:28-29/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r2.claim: Being dead means being sperm, and being brought to life means being created; Muqatil links this life-from-death wording to 30:19.
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r2.anchor: { وكنتم أمواتا } ، يعنى نطفا، { فأحياكم } ، يعنى فخلقكم،

MUQATIL:2:28-29/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r3.claim: God causes death after life, raises people after death on Resurrection Day, and returns them to Him for recompense according to their deeds.
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r3.anchor: { ثم يميتكم } عند إحيائكم، { ثم يحييكم } من بعد الموت يوم القيامة،

MUQATIL:2:28-29/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r4.claim: Muqatil says the Jews recognized the truth and stayed silent, while the polytheists objected that nobody could raise them after they became dust; this prompted the next verse.
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r4.anchor: فأما اليهود، فعرفوا وسكتوا، وأما المشركون، فقالوا: أئذا كنا ترابا، من يقدر أن يبعثنا من بعد الموت؟

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r1.claim: The question expresses denial and astonishment: how disbelieve when the account gives reasons to believe? It resembles asking whether someone can fly without wings.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r1.anchor: معنى الهمزة التى في كيف مثله فى قولك اتكفرون بالله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r2.claim: They were lifeless sperm drops in their fathers’ loins; ميت can also describe anything devoid of life, as in 25:49.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r2.anchor: نطفا فى أصلاب آبائكم والواو للحال وقد مضمرة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r3.claim: The waw is circumstantial with قد understood; أموات is the plural of ميت, like أقوال from قول.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r3.anchor: والاموات جمع ميت كالأقوال جمع قول

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r4.claim: God gives life in the womb, causes death when lifetimes end, and raises people for resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r4.anchor: ﴿ فأحياكم ﴾ فى الأرحام ﴿ ثم يميتكم ﴾ عند انقضاء آجالكم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r5.claim: Return may mean arrival at recompense; alternatively the second life is in the graves and the return is resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r5.anchor: فى قبوركم ثم إليه ترجعون للنشور

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r6.claim: Fa marks the immediate first life, while thumma marks the delays before death, the second life, and return to judgment.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r6.anchor: لأن الإحياء الأول قد تعقب الموت بلا تراخ

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#2/r7.claim: The account contains clear signs that should turn people away from disbelief and great blessings that should be thanked, not denied.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r1.claim: كيف asks about a state, is accusative with تكفرون, and is built on fatḥa; although its astonished interrogative force suggests a particle and an expected sukūn, fatḥa was chosen for ease.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r1.anchor: «كيف» سؤال عن الحال، وهي اسم في موضع نصب ب «تكفرون»، وهي مبنية على الفتح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r2.claim: The address expresses astonishment that people deny despite having conclusive proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r2.anchor: أي هؤلاء ممن يجب أن يتعجب منهم حين كفروا وقد ثبتت عليهم الحجة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r3.claim: The address can reach the People of the Book because rejecting Muhammad and his message means denying God’s revelation of the Qur’an; saying the Qur’an is human speech is associating partners with God and breaking the covenant.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r3.anchor: لما لم يثبتوا أمر محمد عليه السلام ولم يصدقوه فيما جاء به فقد أشركوا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r4.claim: Another explanation takes كيف as a declarative rebuke, not a real question: how can you deny God’s favors and power?
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r4.anchor: وقيل: «كيف» لفظه لفظ الاستفهام وليس به، بل هو تقرير وتوبيخ أي كيف تكفرون نعمه عليكم وقدرته هذه!

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r5.speaker: الواسطي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r5.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says this is the strongest rebuke: inanimate matter does not dispute with its maker; dispute comes only from spiritual forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r5.anchor: قال الواسطي: وبخهم بهذا غاية التوبيخ لأن الموات والجماد لا ينازع صانعه في شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r6.claim: The wāw in وكنتم is circumstantial, with قد omitted; al-Zajjāj reconstructs وقد كنتم.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r6.anchor: هذه الواو واو الحال، وقد مضمرة. قال الزجاج: التقدير وقد كنتم، ثم حذفت قد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ parses أمواتا as the predicate of كنتم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r8.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r8.claim: Abu Ḥātim treats the pause after فأحياكم ثم يميتكم as a complete pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r8.anchor: هذا وقف التمام كذا قال أبو حاتم. ثم قال: { ثم يحييكم }

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r9.claim: They explain the sequence as nonexistence before creation, worldly life, death at the end of the term, and resurrection; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this is the intended meaning, since unbelievers accept the first three stages and have no proof for denying resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r9.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وابن مسعود: أي كنتم أمواتا معدومين قبل أن تخلقوا فأحياكم أي خلقكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r10.claim: On the preceding interpretation, some count life in the grave as part of worldly life; others do not count it, just as an intervening worldly death is not counted when someone is revived in this life.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r10.anchor: وقيل: لم يعتد بها كما لم يعتد بموت من أماته في الدنيا ثم أحياه في الدنيا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r11.claim: Another view places people in Adam’s loins, then as particles drawn from him, followed by worldly death and resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r11.anchor: وقيل { وكنتم أمواتا }: أي نطفا في أصلاب الرجال وأرحام النساء، ثم نقلكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r12.claim: Another view counts existence as sperm in loins and wombs, worldly life, death, life and questioning in the grave, death there, then resurrection life that has no later death; Qurtubi counts three deaths and three lives.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r12.anchor: قلت: فعلى هذا التأويل هي ثلاث موتات، وثلاث إحياءات.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r13.claim: Counting Adamic existence and extraction with testimony separately from the sperm stage yields four deaths and four lives; another view adds a pre-Adamic creation like dust and death, yielding five of each.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28/r13.anchor: فعلى هذا تجيء أربع موتات وأربع إحياءات. وقد قيل: إن الله تعالى أوجدهم قبل خلق آدم عليه السلام كالهباء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r1.claim: Muslim transmits Abu Saʿīd’s report that ordinary inhabitants of the Fire neither die nor live, but sinful believers are killed by the Fire until charcoal, then intercession brings them in groups to Paradise’s rivers, where they grow like seeds carried by a flood; a listener remarks that the Prophet must have herded sheep in the desert.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r1.anchor: وموتة سادسة للعصاة من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دخلوا النار لحديث أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r2.claim: Qurtubi takes فأماتهم الله literally, since the verbal noun emphasizes real death and this honors the believers; the alternative is that it means sleep-like concealment from pain, but he prefers the literal sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r2.anchor: قلت: فقوله «فأماتهم الله» حقيقة في الموت لأنه أكده بالمصدر، وذلك تكريما لهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r3.claim: Grammarians agree that emphasizing a verb with its verbal noun makes it literal, not metaphorical; Qurtubi cites 4:164 as an example.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r3.anchor: وقد أجمع النحويون على أنك إذا أكدت الفعل بالمصدر لم يكن مجازا، وإنما هو على الحقيقة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes being dead as obscurity, being brought to life as gaining remembrance and honor through Islam and its Prophet, then losing that remembrance in death before resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: المعنى وكنتم أمواتا بالخمول فأحياكم بأن ذكرتم وشرفتم بهذا الدين والنبي الذي جاءكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r5.claim: The return is to God’s punishment because of disbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ثم إليه ترجعون } أي إلى عذابه مرجعكم لكفركم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r6.claim: Another explanation takes the return as renewed life and questioning, since restoration is like the first creation, as stated in 21:104.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: إلى الحياة وإلى المسألة كما قال تعالى: كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r7.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق ومجاهد وابن محيصن وسلام بن يعقوب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r7.claim: The common reading is ترجعون; these readers open the imperfect prefix and kasra the jīm wherever this form occurs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:28#2/r7.anchor: ويحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق ومجاهد وابن محيصن وسلام بن يعقوب يفتحون حرف المضارعة ويكسرون الجيم

QASHANI:2:28-29/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r1.claim: The question asks how they can be veiled from God.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r1.anchor: أي: على أي حال تحجبون عنه

QASHANI:2:28-29/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r2.claim: Being dead refers to semen in the fathers' loins; their creation should lead them to infer the Creator.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r2.anchor: أي: لم لا تستدلون بالخلق على الخالق

QASHANI:2:28-29/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r3.claim: Ordinarily this is natural death, resurrection, and return for recompense; the first creation is observable and supports inference to resurrection.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r3.anchor: إذ الأول معلوم بالمشاهدة، والثاني بالاستدلال عليه بالإنشاء الأول

QASHANI:2:28-29/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r4.claim: Alternatively, death is voluntary annihilation of the self in unity, followed by true life as abiding through the Real's bestowed existence.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r4.anchor: بالموت الإرادي الذي هو الفناء في الوحدة ثم يحييكم بالحياة الحقيقية التي هي البقاء بعد الفناء

QASHANI:2:28-29/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r5.claim: Return means witnessing if unity is of the attributes, or vision if unity is of the Essence.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r5.anchor: للمشاهدة إن كانت الوحدة وحدة الصفات، أو الشهود إن كانت وحدة الذات

RAZI-FULL:v2p128/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p128/r1.speaker: قالوا
RAZI-FULL:v2p128/r1.claim: They argue that if God misleads as Satan does, God deserves blame and refuge; Satan’s lack of causal power would shift all responsibility for misguidance to God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p128/r1.anchor: قالوا بل خصيصية الله تعالى في ذلك أكثر إذ تضليل إبليس سواء وجوده وعدمه فيما يرجع إلى حصول الضلال

RAZI-FULL:v2p128/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p128/r2.speaker: قالوا
RAZI-FULL:v2p128/r2.claim: They argue that God attributes misguidance to Pharaoh, the Samaritan, people, and Satan; if God alone caused it, blaming them is false, and shared causation makes their blame unjust.
RAZI-FULL:v2p128/r2.anchor: وسادسها : أنه تعالى أضاف الإضلال عن الدين إلى غيره وذمهم لأجل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r1.claim: Rāzī frames 2:28–40 as an account of four blessings common to all accountable people; life is the first, before the blessings of earth and sky.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r1.anchor: من هذا الموضع إلى قوله : { خالدون يابنى إسراءيل اذكروا نعمتي

RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r2.claim: The interrogative “How can you disbelieve?” is a rebuke, since the greater a benefaction, the graver the recipient’s disobedience; God recalls His immense gifts to deter disbelief and prompt faith.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r2.anchor: وإن كان بصورة الاستخبار فالمراد به التبكيت والتعنيف ، لأن عظم النعمة يقتضي

RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r3.claim: Life is the foundational blessing and the passage’s central point; Rāzī compares the obligation owed to a benefactor with a child’s greater duty to a nurturing parent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r3.anchor: فذكر تعالى من نعمه ما هو الأصل في النعم وهو الأحياء ، فهذا هو المقصود الكلي

RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r4.claim: The first transition uses fa because life may follow death without delay; thumma marks the delay between life and death and, if resurrection is meant, between death and renewed life.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138/r4.anchor: لأن الأحياء الأول قد يعقب الموت بغير تراخ ، وأما الموت فقد تراخى عن الأحياء

RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r1.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that if God creates unbelief, reproaching people for it is as incoherent as reproaching them for God-created color or illness.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r1.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن الكفر من قبل العباد من وجوه :

RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r2.claim: They argue that if God created people destined for misery and Hell and intended their unbelief, He could not coherently rebuke them for disbelieving.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r2.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن الكفر من قبل العباد من وجوه :

RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r3.claim: They argue that God cannot demand belief while creating unbelief and blocking faith; such address would be mockery rather than proof against people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r3.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن الكفر من قبل العباد من وجوه :

RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r4.claim: They list foreknowledge, divine will, creation of unbelief, and created capacities and volitions as six causes of unbelief, with six corresponding causes of faith absent, making belief impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r4.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن الكفر من قبل العباد من وجوه :

RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r5.claim: They argue that under compulsion life is no benefaction if God intends to lead an unbeliever to eternal Hell, just as poisoned food is not a gift despite its pleasant appearance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r5.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن الكفر من قبل العباد من وجوه :

RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r6.claim: Rāzī answers that the objections rely on praise, blame, commands, and punishment; divine foreknowledge makes an act contrary to what God knows impossible without making the rebuke incoherent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r6.anchor: فنحن أيضا نقابلها بالكلام المعتمد في هذه الشبهة ، وهو أن الله سبحانه وتعالى علم

RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r7.claim: He adds that a capacity suited to either belief or unbelief needs a determinant; if the servant supplies it the regress returns, while a divine determinant makes the act necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v2p138#2/r7.anchor: وأيضا فالقدرة على الكفر إن كانت صالحة للإيمان امتنع كونها مصدرا للإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r1.claim: All agree that “you were dead” refers to being earth and semen: Adam began from earth, and the other accountable descendants, except Jesus, from semen.
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r1.anchor: اتفقوا على أن قوله : { وكنتم أمواتا } المراد به وكنتم ترابا ونطفا

RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r2.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r2.claim: Most scholars say applying “dead” to inanimate matter is figurative: a dead being has undergone death and normally was capable of life, unlike inert matter.
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r2.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه مجاز لأنه شبه الموات بالميت وليس أحدهما من الآخر بسبيل

RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r3.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r3.claim: Qatāda takes “dead” literally: people were dead in their fathers’ loins, God enlivened and brought them forth, then caused their necessary death and raised them; this yields two lives and two deaths.
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r3.anchor: وهو مروي عن قتادة ، قال كانوا أمواتا في أصلاب آبائهم فأحياهم الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r4.claim: Rāzī prefers the figurative reading: Arabic calls inert matter mawāt, not mayyit, and mayyit ordinarily implies something that could have lived.
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r4.anchor: والأول هو الأقرب ، لأنه يقال في الجماد إنه موات وليس بميت

RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r5.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r5.claim: Al-Qaffāl compares the phrase to 76:1: humans were nothing remembered, with “dead” used figuratively for something obscure or without a mention.
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r5.anchor: قال القفال : وهو كقوله تعالى : { هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا }

RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r6.speaker: المخبل السعدي
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r6.claim: Al-Mukhabbal al-Saʿdī’s line illustrates metaphorical life and death of remembrance: some memories remain dormant, while others are more vivid.
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r6.anchor: قال المخبل السعدي : فوأحييت لي ذكرى وما خاملا … ولكن بعض الذكر أنبه من بعض …

RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r7.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r7.claim: Some argue that the verse allows only earthly life and resurrection, with two deaths and two lives, so it excludes an intermediate life and punishment in the grave.
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r7.anchor: احتج قوم بهذه الآية على بطلان عذاب القبر ، قالوا لأنه تعالى بين أنه يحييهم مرة

RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r8.claim: Rāzī replies that omission of grave life does not prove its absence; indeed, “then you return to Him” may follow a distinct, non-eternal life in the grave.
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r8.anchor: لم يلزم من عدم الذكر في هذه الآية أن لا تكون حاصلة

RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r9.claim: The proposed appeal to 40:11 is disputed because it is speech by the disbelievers; a pre-world life of the progeny in Adam could already supply two lives and deaths without grave life.
RAZI-FULL:v2p139/r9.anchor: لأنه قول الكفار ، ولأن كثيرا من الناس أثبتوا حياة الذر في حلب آدم

RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r1.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the address concerns people generally; some individuals, however, experienced three deaths and revivals in exceptional events.
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r1.anchor: قال الحسن رحمه الله قوله : { كيف تكفرون بالله } يعني به العامة ، وأما

RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r2.claim: Rāzī cites the man at the ruined town, those fleeing death, the Israelites struck by lightning, the slain man revived by the cow, and the sleepers of the cave as exceptional cases.
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r2.anchor: وأما بعض الناس فقد أماتهم ثلاث مرات نحو ما حكى في قوله

RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r3.speaker: المجسمة
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r3.claim: Corporealists take “you return to Him” to mean that God occupies a place to which people return.
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r3.anchor: تمسك المجسمة بقوله تعالى : { ثم إليه ترجعون } على أنه تعالى في مكان

RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r4.claim: Rāzī says the return is to God’s judgment and exclusive authority: He raises the dead and gathers them, as when one says that a matter returns to the prince.
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r4.anchor: والمراد أنهم إلى حكمه يرجعون لأنه تعالى يبعث من في القبور ويجمعهم في المحشر

RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r5.claim: The verse proves that only God can give life and death, refuting natural philosophers who assign these effects to stars, elements, or temperaments.
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r5.anchor: أنها دالة على أنه لا يقدر على الإحياء والإماتة إلا الله تعالى فيبطل به قول أهل الطبائع

RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r6.claim: God’s first revival of dead matter supplies a rational indication that He can resurrect it again.
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r6.anchor: أنها تدل على صحة الحشر النشر مع التنبيه على الدليل العقلي الدال عليه

RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r7.claim: The life-and-death sequence also establishes accountability, encouragement, and warning.
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r7.anchor: الثالث : أنها تدل على التكليف والترغيب والترهيب .

RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r8.claim: Rāzī says the verse indicates both compulsion and human acquisition, referring back to the preceding discussion of divine determination.
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r8.anchor: الرابع : أنها دالة على الجبر والقدر كما تقدم بيانه ، الخامس : أنها دالة على وجوب الزهد في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r9.claim: The verse teaches detachment from worldly life: God develops a person from semen, grants faculties and possessions, then removes them in death and leaves the body forgotten in its grave.
RAZI-FULL:v2p140/r9.anchor: فبين أنه لا بد من الموت ثم بين أنه لا يترك على هذا الموت

RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r1.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r1.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh al-Rāzī pictures relatives passing the grave as if they had never known the deceased, illustrating the loneliness of death.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r1.anchor: فيمر أقاربي بحذاء قبري … كأن أقاربي لم يعرفوني

RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r2.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r2.claim: His prayer imagines the deceased abandoned in the grave and asks God, the source of ancient kindness, for mercy and forgiveness there.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r2.anchor: وقال أيضا : إلهي كأني بنفسي وقد أضجعوها في حفرتها

RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r3.claim: Rāzī describes the final return: the trumpet is blown, the dead rise from graves, stand before God, and fall silent in awe.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r3.anchor: يأمر بأن ينفخ في الصور { فصعق من فى * السماوات * ومن فى الارض

RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r4.claim: An unnamed supplicant asks God not to turn away from people resurrected frightened, hungry, exposed, burdened by sins, bewildered, and regretful.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إلهنا إذا قمنا من ثرى الأجداث مغبرة رؤوسنا

QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r8.claim: The opening is an exclamation of astonishment: with signs made manifest, the heart should not incline toward disbelief.
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r8.anchor: هذه كلمة تعجيب وتعظيم لما فيه العبد ، أي لا ينبغي

QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r9.claim: God made Himself known to creatures through the luminous indications and brilliant signs of His power.
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r9.anchor: ويقال تعرف إلى الخلق بلوائح دلالاته ، ولوامع آياته

QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r10.claim: The dead are the initially undifferentiated sperm; life differentiates its parts into bone, flesh, hair, skin, and other bodily forms.

QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r11.claim: Death reduces people to bones and dust; resurrection gathers them, and return is to the decree already made concerning their felicity or wretchedness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r11.anchor: ثم يميتكم } بأن يجعلكم عظاما ورفاتا ، { ثم يحييكم

QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r12.claim: In an inward reading, spiritual death is ignorance of God and life is knowing Him; death then means removal from one's own witnessing, followed by revival as God takes one beyond the self.
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r12.anchor: بجهلكم عنا ، ثم { فأحياكم } بمعرفتكم بنا

QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r13.claim: This reading makes the return to God the keeping of sacred-law rulings through the enactment of the Real.
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r13.anchor: إليه ترجعون } أي بحفظ أحكام الشرع بإجراء الحق

QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r14.claim: Another reading calls persistence of the self death and its annihilation life; God then removes the servant from witnessing that state and revives him by taking him from himself.

QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r15.claim: The servant's final return is described as being turned about within God's grasp.
QUSHAYRI:v1p31/r15.anchor: ثم إليه ترجعون بتقلبكم في قبضته سبحانه وتعالى

QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r1.claim: God keeps the realized in alternating states, not permanent life or total annihilation: subsistence and extinction, affirmation and negation, sobriety and effacement succeed one another.
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r1.anchor: فهم أبدا بين نفي وإثبات ، وبين بقاء وفناء ، وبين صحو ومحو

STUDYQURAN:2:28/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r1.claim: The four stages are existence before birth, earthly life, earthly death, and resurrection; 40:11 similarly speaks of dying and living twice.
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r1.anchor: The four stages mentioned here are before birth, during earthly life, earthly death, and resurrection.

STUDYQURAN:2:28/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r2.claim: One interpretation takes the initial dead state as material existence in the body, in the parents’ loins, or as dust of the earth.
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r2.anchor: understood either as one’s “existence” in the material stuff of the body, literally in the loins of one’s parents or the dust of the earth

STUDYQURAN:2:28/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r3.claim: The alternative is an unremembered or unknown state: Arabs call something dead when its traces are effaced and it is no longer mentioned or remembered.

STUDYQURAN:2:28/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r4.claim: Both readings refer to our nonexistence before worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r4.anchor: before our life in this world.

STUDYQURAN:2:28/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r5.speaker: Ibn ʿArabī
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r5.claim: Ibn ʿArabī understands pre-earthly lifelessness as nonmanifestation within God’s Knowledge, not ordinary nothingness; life first gives form to what eternally exists in that Knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:2:28/r5.anchor: Someone like the Sufi mystic IbnʿArabī (d. 638/1240) would understand the “lifelessness” of our pre-earthly condition to be a state of nonmanifestation within God’s Knowledge

TAB-FULL:v1p444/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r1.speaker: أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r1.claim: A report from a group of the Prophet's Companions says people were nothing, then God created them, caused their death, and will raise them on Resurrection Day.
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r1.anchor: عن ناس، من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

TAB-FULL:v1p444/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r2.claim: Abdullah equates the two deaths and two lives in 40:11 with the sequence described in this verse.
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله: " في قوله: {أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} [غافر: 11] قال: هي كالتي في البقرة:

TAB-FULL:v1p444/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r3.claim: Abu Malik says God created them when they were nothing, then caused them to die and revived them; another report of his describes them as dead before God gave them life.
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r3.anchor: عن أبي مالك: " في قوله: {أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} [غافر: 11] قال: خلقتنا ولم نكن شيئا، ثم أمتنا، ثم أحييتنا "

TAB-FULL:v1p444/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r4.claim: Mujahid says they were nothing when created, then undergo the true death and are revived; he calls the wording in 40:11 equivalent.
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: " في قوله: {كيف تكفرون بالله

TAB-FULL:v1p444/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the passage about two deaths and two lives in 40:11 with the sequence in this verse.
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " هو قوله: {أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} [غافر: 11] "

TAB-FULL:v1p444/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliya says God created them when they were nothing, then raised them, caused their death, and raised them at Resurrection; after that they return to Him.
TAB-FULL:v1p444/r6.anchor: قال: حدثني أبو العالية: " في قول الله: {كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا} [البقرة: 28] يقول: حين لم يكونوا شيئا

TAB-FULL:v1p445/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by al-Dahhak, counts being dust before creation as the first death, creation as life, death in the grave as the second death, and resurrection as the second life.
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " في قوله: {أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} [غافر: 11] قال: كنتم ترابا قبل أن يخلقكم

TAB-FULL:v1p445/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r2.claim: Abu Salih's report from al-Suddi says that God gives life in the grave and then causes death.
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r2.anchor: عن السدي، عن أبي صالح: " {كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا

TAB-FULL:v1p445/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r3.claim: Qatada says they were lifeless semen in their fathers' loins, then God created them, caused the necessary death, and will raise them for Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: " قوله: {كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا} [البقرة: 28] الآية. قال: كانوا أمواتا في أصلاب آبائهم

TAB-FULL:v1p445/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the deaths and lives through the primordial covenant: God extracted Adam's descendants, gave them awareness and took their pledge, then formed them in wombs, caused death, and will raise them. He links this to 40:11, 7:172–173, 4:1, 39:6, 4:154, and 5:7.
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " في قول الله تعالى: {ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} [غافر: 11] قال: خلقهم من ظهر آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p445/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r5.claim: Al-Tabari says each of the interpretations he has transmitted has an interpretive basis and approach.
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r5.anchor: ولكل قول من هذه الأقوال التي حكيناها عمن رويناها عنه وجه ومذهب من التأويل

TAB-FULL:v1p445/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r6.claim: Arabic calls a vanished or obscure matter dead because its trace and mention have faded; a living matter is salient and known among people.
TAB-FULL:v1p445/r6.anchor: هذا شيء ميت، وهذا أمر ميت؛ يراد بوصفه بالموت خمول ذكره ودروس أثره من الناس.

TAB-FULL:v1p448/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r1.claim: Al-Tabari cites Abu Nukhayla's poem: reviving remembrance means making it famous, contrasting obscurity with a mention that is especially resonant.
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r1.anchor: فأحييت لي ذكري وما كنت خاملا

TAB-FULL:v1p448/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r2.claim: On the reading that 'dead' means unremembered, people were obscure in their fathers' loins, became known as living humans, died back into obscurity, and will be bodily restored with souls so they recognize one another at resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r2.anchor: فكذلك تأويل قول من قال في قوله: {وكنتم أمواتا} [البقرة: 28] لم تكونوا شيئا: أي كنتم خمولا لا ذكر لكم

TAB-FULL:v1p448/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r3.claim: It is far-fetched to address people after they have been revived in their graves: the verse reproaches them for past crimes to call them back to repentance, which is impossible after death.
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r3.anchor: ولا إنابة في القبور بعد الممات ولا توبة فيها بعد الوفاة.

TAB-FULL:v1p448/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r4.claim: Qatada's reading takes the first state as semen without souls, the first life as the breathing of souls into it, death as the soul's departure, and the final life as resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v1p448/r4.anchor: فإنه عنى بذلك أنهم كانوا نطفا لا أرواح فيها

TAB-FULL:v1p450/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd's account entails three lives and three deaths; al-Tabari rejects it as contrary to the text's two lives and two deaths and notes that no one claims an additional death at the covenant extraction.
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r1.anchor: وزعم ابن زيد في تفسيره أن الله أحياهم ثلاث إحياءات، وأماتهم ثلاث إماتات.

TAB-FULL:v1p450/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r2.claim: Another view counts semen's departure from the man's body as the first death, its ensoulment and formation as life, death as the soul's departure, and resurrection as the second life.
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الموتة الأولى: مفارقة نطفة الرجل جسده إلى رحم المرأة

TAB-FULL:v1p450/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r3.claim: Al-Tabari treats the semen-departure account as a possible interpretation only if it had been held by a recognized authority whose Qur'anic interpretation is trusted.
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r3.anchor: وهذا قول ووجه من التأويل لو كان به قائل من أهل القدوة الذين يرتضى للقرآن تأويلهم

TAB-FULL:v1p450/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas's reading: unremembered embryos became known as humans, died into unrecognized remains in the barzakh, and will be raised with souls before returning to God.
TAB-FULL:v1p450/r4.anchor: القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن مسعود، وعن ابن عباس، من أن معنى قوله: {وكنتم أمواتا} [البقرة: 28] أموات الذكر خمولا في أصلاب آبائكم

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r1.claim: Al-Tabari links the return and gathering to the resurrection scene in 36:51, where after the horn is blown people emerge from the graves toward their Lord.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r1.anchor: ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r2.claim: The verse reproves hypocrites who profess belief in God and the Last Day while inwardly disbelieving and using the profession to deceive God and the believers.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r2.anchor: هذه الآية توبيخ من الله جل ثناؤه للقائلين: {آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر} [البقرة: 8] الذين أخبر الله عنهم أنهم مع قيلهم ذلك بأفواههم غير مؤمنين به

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r3.claim: Al-Tabari argues that the question challenges their denial of God's power to revive them after death, restore them after annihilation, and gather them for recompense.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r3.anchor: كيف تكفرون بالله فتجحدون قدرته على إحيائكم بعد إماتتكم وإعادتكم بعد إفنائكم

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r4.claim: God reminds hypocrites and Jewish scholars of past favors despite their sins, warning of punishment like that of their predecessors while urging repentance for salvation at Judgment; he links their story to the warning at 2:6.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r4.anchor: يحذرهم بذلك تعجيل العقوبة لهم كالتي عجلها للأسلاف والأفراط قبلهم، ويخوفهم حلول مثلاته بساحتهم

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r5.claim: The following account of Adam shows God's honor to humanity, the consequences of disobedience for Adam and Iblis, mercy for Adam's repentance, and punishment for Iblis's pride and refusal to repent.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r5.anchor: فبدأ بعد تعديده عليهم ما عدد من نعمه التي هم فيها مقيمون بذكر أبينا وأبيهم آدم أبي البشر، صلوات الله عليه، وما سلف منه من كرامته إليه وآلائه لديه

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r6.claim: These stories address the People of the Book, who know them from their scriptures, and serve as evidence to them that Muhammad is God's messenger: he could not have learned their hidden accounts from books or their community.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r6.anchor: وخاصا أهل الكتاب بما ذكر من قصص آدم وسائر القصص التي ذكرها معها وبعدها مما علمه أهل الكتاب وجهلته الأمة الأمية

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r11.claim: God made them living humans after they were semen in their fathers' loins, will kill and raise them for reward or punishment, and provides earthly livelihoods and proofs of His oneness.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r11.anchor: فمعنى الكلام إذا: كيف تكفرون بالله وقد كنتم نطفا في أصلاب آبائكم، فجعلكم بشرا أحياء، ثم يميتكم

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r12.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r12.claim: Kayfa expresses astonishment and reproach rather than a genuine question, as in the Qur'anic phrase 'Where are you going?'
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r12.anchor: وكيف بمعنى التعجب والتوبيخ لا بمعنى الاستفهام، كأنه قال: ويحكم كيف تكفرون بالله، كما قال: {فأين تذهبون} [التكوير: 26]

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r13.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r13.claim: The past-tense clause functions circumstantially, with an understood qad omitted because the context signals it, as in 4:90 and ordinary Arabic usage.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r13.anchor: وحل قوله: {وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم} [البقرة: 28] محل الحال، وفيه إضمار قد، ولكنها حذفت لما في الكلام من الدليل عليها.

SULAMI:v1p53/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p53/r1.claim: They were dead through associating partners with God and were brought to life through tawhid.
SULAMI:v1p53/r1.anchor: قيل فيه كنتم أمواتا بالشرك وأحياكم بالتوحيد

SULAMI:v1p53/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p53/r2.claim: Death here is ignorance, and life is knowledge.
SULAMI:v1p53/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : كنتم أمواتا بالجهل فأحياكم بالعلم

SULAMI:v1p53/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53/r3.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p53/r3.claim: Death is discord, while life is concord.
SULAMI:v1p53/r3.anchor: وقيل فيه : كنتم أمواتا بالخلاف فأحياكم بالائتلاف

SULAMI:v1p53/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53/r4.speaker: بعض البغداديين
SULAMI:v1p53/r4.claim: Life of the self is death; God revives people by causing their selves to die and their hearts to live.
SULAMI:v1p53/r4.anchor: قال بعض البغداديين : كنتم أمواتا بحياة نفوسكم فأحياكم بإماتة نفوسكم وإحياء قلوبكم

SULAMI:v1p53/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53/r5.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v1p53/r5.claim: They were dead apart from Him and He gave them life through Him.
SULAMI:v1p53/r5.anchor: وقال الشبلي : كنتم أمواتا عنه فأحياكم به

SULAMI:v1p53/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p53/r6.claim: Death is life at the outward level; life comes through unveiling the innermost secrets.
SULAMI:v1p53/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : كنتم أمواتا بالظواهر فأحياكم بمكاشفة السرائر

SULAMI:v1p53/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53/r7.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v1p53/r7.claim: They die to their own witnessing, live by His witnessing, then die to that witnessing and live through God's standing; they return from what is theirs to what belongs to Him.
SULAMI:v1p53/r7.anchor: وقال فارس : كنتم أمواتا بشواهدكم فأحياكم بشاهده ثم يميتكم عن شواهدكم ثم يحييكم بقيام الحق عنه

SULAMI:v1p53/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53/r8.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p53/r8.claim: This is the culmination of rebuke: inanimate things do not contest what is illumined; opposition comes from spiritual forms.
SULAMI:v1p53/r8.anchor: قال الواسطي : ويختم بها غاية التوبيخ لأن الموات والجماد لا ينازع ما نور في شيء

TABATABAI:2:28-29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r1.claim: This is a second return to the opening call: after summarizing it in 2:21, the passage expands over twelve verses on humanity's nature, gifts, and journey.
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r1.anchor: بيان رجوع ثان إلى ما في بدء الكلام فإنه تعالى بعد ما بين في أول السورة

TABATABAI:2:28-29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r2.claim: The passage rebukes and reminds people of God's favors: He brings them from death to life, through further death and life to return, and grants creation, the earth, the heavens, succession, angelic honor, the Garden, repentance, worship, and guidance.
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r2.anchor: وفيه ذكر جمل ما خص الله تعالى به الإنسان من مواهب التكوين والتشريع

TABATABAI:2:28-29/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r3.claim: The verse supports an intermediate barzakh: the two deaths and two lives in 40:11 require a life between deaths, with the first death after worldly life and the first revival for barzakh.
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r3.anchor: وهذه من الآيات التي يستدل بها على وجود البرزخ بين الدنيا والآخرة

TABATABAI:2:28-29/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r4.speaker: بعض المنكرين للبرزخ
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r4.claim: Some deniers of barzakh argue that 2:28 and 40:11 describe the same two deaths and two lives, so the first death is pre-worldly and neither verse establishes barzakh.
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r4.anchor: وربما ذكر بعض المنكرين للبرزخ أن الآيتين أعني قوله { كيف تكفرون } الآية، وقوله

TABATABAI:2:28-29/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r5.claim: The contexts differ: 2:28 has one death, one causing of death, and two lives, while 40:11 has two acts of causing death; the former's first death is before worldly life, unlike 40:11's first death after it, and the later return is a further stage.
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r5.anchor: فإن الآيتين مختلفتان سياقا إذ المأخوذ في الآية الأولى، موت واحد وإماتة واحدة وإحياءان، وفي الآية الثانية إماتتان وإحياءان

TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r1.claim: Human existence is developmental and transformative: people were lifeless before worldly life, were brought to life by God, and proceed through successive stages of death and life.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r1.anchor: بيان حقيقة الإنسان من حيث وجوده فهو وجود متحول متكامل يسير في مسير وجوده المتبدل المتغير تدريجا

TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r2.claim: The Qur'an portrays humanity as part of the earth, developing through stages into a new creation; the Angel of Death takes the person from the body and the person returns to God.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r2.anchor: تدل على أن الإنسان جزء من الأرض غير مفارقها ولا مباين معها

TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r3.claim: Humans and other natural beings are formed in relations of acting and being acted upon that sustain existence, but humanity has a broader range of action.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r3.anchor: وكل موجود من الموجودات الطبيعية كذلك، أي إنه مفطور على الارتباط مع غيره ليفعل وينفعل ويستبقي به موهبة وجوده

TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r4.claim: Human intellect enables complex acts beyond other beings, including composition, destruction, and repair; people imitate or counter nature and benefit from all things, manifesting the subjection of creation to them.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r4.anchor: فهو من جهة تجهيزة بالإدراك والفكر يختص بتصرفات خارجة عن طوق سائر الموجودات بالتفصيل والتركيب والإفساد والإصلاح

TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r2.claim: The Qur'an connects the beginning of human life to cosmic nature and also to God's creative command: humanity develops through material stages yet is directly related to God's dominion and origination.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r2.anchor: غير أن القرآن كما يعد مبدأ حياته الدنيوية آخذة في الشروع من الطبيعة الكونية ومرتبطة بها أحيانا كذلك يربطها بالرب تعالى وتقدس

TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r3.claim: At the return, humanity follows one of two paths: happiness rises toward God, while misery descends to the lowest depths before ending with the Lord, who encompasses both.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r3.anchor: فأما طريق السعادة فهو أقرب الطرق يأخذ في الانتهاء إلى الرفيع الأعلى ولا يزال يصعد الإنسان ويرفعه حتى ينتهي به إلى ربه

TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r4.claim: The Qur'an details pre-worldly, worldly, and post-worldly life only where they bear on guidance, misguidance, happiness, or misery, leaving other details to their proper passages.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r4.anchor: وأما تفصيل القول في حياته قبل الدنيا وفيها وبعد الدنيا فسيأتي كل في محله

TABRISI:2:28/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r1.speaker: يعقوب
TABRISI:2:28/r1.claim: Yaqub reads tarjiʿūn active with fatḥa on tāʾ; the others read it passive, with ḍamma on tāʾ and fatḥa on jīm.
TABRISI:2:28/r1.anchor: قرأ يعقوب ترجعون بفتح التاء على أن الفعل لهم والباقون بضم التاء وفتح الجيم

TABRISI:2:28/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28/r2.claim: كيف asks about a state and here encompasses every state, as كم covers numbers, ما kinds, أين places, and من rational beings.
TABRISI:2:28/r2.anchor: فكيف ينتظم جميع الأحوال كما أن كم ينتظم جميع العدد وما ينتظم جميع الجنس

TABRISI:2:28/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28/r3.claim: On the reproach reading, the implied question asks whether they disbelieve while relying on a proof; the phrase is a circumstantial accusative governed by تكفرون.
TABRISI:2:28/r3.anchor: وتقديره أمتعلقين بحجة تكفرون فيكون منصوب الموضع على الحال والعامل فيه تكفرون

TABRISI:2:28/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28/r4.claim: One explanation takes كيف as reproach: how can they deny God after He has favored them?
TABRISI:2:28/r4.anchor: ومن قال هو توبيخ قال معناه ويحكم كيف تكفرون

TABRISI:2:28/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r5.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:28/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes the question as astonishment for listeners: marvel that people disbelieve despite God's decisive signs and proofs.
TABRISI:2:28/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج هو استفهام في معنى التعجب وهذا التعجب إنما هو للخلق أو للمؤمنين

TABRISI:2:28/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28/r6.claim: The circumstantial waw means “when you had been”; قد can be implicit with a past verb because a past tense alone cannot serve as a circumstance.
TABRISI:2:28/r6.anchor: ومعنى وكنتم وقد كنتم والواو واو الحال وإضمار قد جائز إذا كان في الكلام دليل عليه

TABRISI:2:28/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28/r7.claim: The same implicit قد is understood in the circumstantial phrase حصرت صدورهم, cited at 4:90.
TABRISI:2:28/r7.anchor: أي قد حصرت صدورهم وهي جملة في موضع الحال

TABRISI:2:28/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28/r8.claim: The verse resumes the argument against deniers of resurrection, messengers, and scriptures by recalling God's favors.
TABRISI:2:28/r8.anchor: ثم عاد الله تعالى إلى الاحتجاج على الكفار في إنكارهم البعث وجحودهم لرسله وكتبه

TABRISI:2:28/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r9.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:28/r9.claim: One view is that people were sperm in their fathers' loins, given life, then died and were resurrected, making two lives and two deaths.
TABRISI:2:28/r9.anchor: ثم عاد الله تعالى إلى الاحتجاج على الكفار في إنكارهم البعث

TABRISI:2:28/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
TABRISI:2:28/r10.claim: Another view is that people were nothing, then created, then will die and be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.
TABRISI:2:28/r10.anchor: لم تكونوا شيئا فخلقكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم يوم القيامة عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود

TABRISI:2:28/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28/r11.claim: A third view uses “dead” for obscurity and “alive” for fame: Arabs call an unknown person dead and a famous person alive, as Abu Nukhayla al-Saʿdi's verse shows.
TABRISI:2:28/r11.anchor: والعرب تسمي كل امرئ خامل ميتا وكل امرئ مشهور حيا كما قال أبو نخيلة السعدي

TABRISI:2:28#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28#2/r1.speaker: أبو نخيلة السعدي
TABRISI:2:28#2/r1.claim: Abu Nukhayla's line uses “I revived what was obscure in my memory” to illustrate fame as life.
TABRISI:2:28#2/r1.anchor: فأحييت من ذكري وما كان خاملا

TABRISI:2:28#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28#2/r2.claim: A fourth view is sperm in parents' bodies, brought into worldly life, then dying and being revived in the grave for questioning.
TABRISI:2:28#2/r2.anchor: ورابعها: أن معناه كنتم نطفا في أصلاب آبائكم وبطون أمهاتكم والنطفة موات فأخرجكم إلى دار الدنيا

TABRISI:2:28#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28#2/r3.claim: The final return is resurrection for judgment and recompense; it means exclusive divine jurisdiction, not movement between places, like a people's affair returning to its governor.
TABRISI:2:28#2/r3.anchor: وسمي الحشر رجوعا إلى الله تعالى لأنه رجوع إلى حيث لا يكون أحد يتولى الحكم فيه غير الله

TABRISI:2:28#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28#2/r4.claim: Life is named first because creating a person alive is the first favor and enables enjoyment and benefit.
TABRISI:2:28#2/r4.anchor: لأن أول نعمة أنعم الله بها عليه خلقه إياه حيا لينفعه وبالحياة يتمكن الانسان من الانتفاع

TABRISI:2:28#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28#2/r5.claim: Death is a favor insofar as it ends moral obligation and lets the accountable person reach lasting reward.
TABRISI:2:28#2/r5.anchor: لأن الموت يقطع التكليف فيصل المكلف بعده إلى الثواب الدائم فهو من هذا الوجه نعمة

TABRISI:2:28#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28#2/r6.claim: An alternative says death is mentioned to complete the proof, not because it is a blessing.
TABRISI:2:28#2/r6.anchor: وقيل إنما ذكر الموت لتمام الاحتجاج لا لكونه نعمة

TABRISI:2:28#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:28#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:28#2/r7.claim: The verse supports human responsibility: God neither wills nor creates disbelief in people, since He attributes it to them as their own act.
TABRISI:2:28#2/r7.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أنه تعالى لم يرد من عباده الكفر ولا خلقه فيهم

FARRA:v1p24/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p24/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p24/r5.claim: “Dead” refers to sperm; anything separated from the body, including hair or sperm, is dead.
FARRA:v1p24/r5.anchor: كل ما فارق الجسد من شعر أو نطفة فهو

FARRA:v1p24/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p24/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p24/r6.claim: God brought people to life from sperm, will cause them to die after life, and will revive them for resurrection.
FARRA:v1p24/r6.anchor: فأحياكم من النطف، ثم يميتكم بعد الحياة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r1.claim: How primarily asks about a state and takes a state as its answer; it ranges over all states, as how-many, what, where, when, and who range over numbers, kinds, places, times, and rational beings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r1.anchor: قال النحويون: (كيف) في الأصل سؤال عن الحال، لأن جوابه يكون بالحال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads how as an exclamation addressed to people and believers: they should marvel that these people disbelieve despite God’s established proof.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: تأويل (كيف) هاهنا استفهام في معنى التعجب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r3.claim: Al-Farra reads the question as exclamation and rebuke, not a genuine request for information, comparing it to ‘Where are you going?’ (81:26).
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p288/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: هذا على وجه التعجب والتوبيخ لا على الاستفهام المحض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r1.claim: Kana may be complete, requiring only its subject and meaning ‘occurred’; incomplete, requiring a predicate; or redundant, entering without changing the construction, as in 19:29.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r1.anchor: في الكلام على وجوه: تامة وناقصة وزائدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r2.claim: Incomplete kana inflects like a verb but, strictly, indicates time and enters a subject–predicate construction; kana Zaydun masrūran means Zayd was happy. Its verbal nouns are kawn and kaynūna.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r2.anchor: وليست بفعل على الحقيقة، إنما تدل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r3.claim: Al-Farra explains kaynūna and related verbal nouns: such forms are common from yāʾ verbs but rare from wāw verbs; kaynūna is one of four exceptions, formed by analogy because wāw and yāʾ are close in articulation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: [تقول] (¬6) في ذوات (الياء): الطيرورة والحيدودة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r4.speaker: الخليل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r4.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes kaynūna as fayʿalūla, from kaywanūna, with yāʾ and wāw assimilated and the result then lightened; al-Farra says this is plausible but prefers the first account.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r4.anchor: وكان الخليل يقول: كينونة (فيعلولة)، وهي الأصل (كيونونة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r5.claim: Al-Farra supplies an omitted qad: ‘you had been dead’; without qad the construction would not be grammatical, as in his reading of the Yusuf example, ‘she had lied.’

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r6.claim: Al-Farra says a result or state following another completed event requires qad, expressed or understood, as in ‘your wealth has grown’; the second clause describes the first event’s state.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p289/r6.anchor: وقولك للرجل: أصبحت كثر مالك، لا يجوز إلا وأنت تريد: قد كثر مالك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r1.claim: In a report through al-Dahhak, Ibn Abbas explains ‘dead’ as dust, returning people to their father Adam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك: أراد (¬6): وكنتم ترابا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r2.claim: In a report through ʿAta and al-Kalbi, Ibn Abbas says ‘dead’ means sperm; anything that leaves the body, including semen or hair, is dead.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r2.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء والكلبي: وكنتم نطفا، وكل ما فارق الجسد من نطفة أو شعر فهو ميت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r3.claim: God gave life in the womb by forming people and placing life in them, causes their worldly death, resurrects them, and returns them to act as His prior knowledge and decree determine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p293/r3.anchor: {فأحياكم} في الأرحام بأن خلقكم بشرا، وجعل فيكم الحياة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r1.claim: Being dead before life refers to sperm in the wombs.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r2.claim: Anything that leaves the body, including hair, a nail, or sperm, is considered dead.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r2.anchor: وكل شيء فارق الجسد من شعر أو ظفر أو نطفة فهو ميتة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r3.claim: God gives life to you in the wombs and in worldly life.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r4.claim: The first death is sperm becoming dead upon entering the womb; it is brought to life there and in this world, then dies and is raised at resurrection.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p44#3/r4.anchor: فالميتة الأولى: إخراج النطفة وهي حية من الرجل، فإذا صارت في الرحم فهي ميتة؛

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p278#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p278#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p278#2/r1.claim: كيف asks about a state or manner, equivalent to asking in what condition someone is.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p278#2/r1.anchor: كيف بمعنى: على أي حال، تقول:

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p278#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p278#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p278#2/r2.claim: Here كيف conveys astonishment at people denying God after being dead and then brought to life.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p278#2/r2.anchor: وتقع بمعنى: التعجب، في مثل قوله:

ELMALILI:2:28-29/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r1.claim: Elmalılı says these verses contain the sciences of this world and the hereafter, showing life, its course, and its purpose, as well as the value of human creation before God.
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r1.anchor: Bu iki âyette bütün dünya ve âhiret ilimleri mündericdir. Hayat, cereyân-ı hayât, gāye-i hayât gösteriliyor

ELMALILI:2:28-29/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r3.claim: The passage raises the human spirit from the material and perceptible toward the intelligible, and asks how anyone could turn to disbelief and ingratitude in light of these truths.
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r3.anchor: ve bu hakāik karşısında küfür ve küfrâna nasıl

ELMALILI:2:28-29/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r4.claim: The emphatic rhetorical question powerfully condemns and warns against disbelief and ingratitude; Elmalılı praises the address for its eloquence, purity, sublimity, learning, truth, and moral force.
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r4.anchor: Küfür ve küfrânı takbih ve insanları ondan tahzir için bu istifhamdaki tesirin şiddeti ne kadar büyüktür

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r1.claim: The address reaches all people, especially disbelievers, hypocrites, and sinners: how can they be ungrateful through intellectual or practical disbelief, a condition inconceivable for anyone with knowledge or moral sense?
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r1.anchor: Ey insanlar, insan adını taşıyanlar ve ‘ale’l-husûs ey kefere, ey münafıkīn, ey feseka! Allah’a nasıl nankörlük eder

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r2.claim: All people, individually and collectively, were lifeless before receiving life; they had no inherent possession, being first earth and then a drop in their forefather’s loins.
