ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r2.anchor: siz hepiniz, gerek her biriniz, gerek mecmû‘unuz mukaddemâ hep ölü idiniz, emvât hâlinde idiniz, hayatınız yoktu

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r3.claim: God gave people life and made them embodied, living, thinking humans who breathe, eat, reproduce, sense, think, choose, act, and resist external events through bodily and spiritual powers.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r3.anchor: Allah size hayat verdi, teneffüs, tegaddî, tenasül eder, duyar, düşünür, ister, istediği yere gider, istediği işi yapar

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r4.claim: Life is not a person’s own property: people cannot even change the color of a single hair, and remembering their former and future states shows that their life was given to them.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r4.anchor: bu hayat sizin kendi malınız olmadığını anlarsınız. O hâlde bu hayatı size bahşeden Allah teâlâ’yı nasıl inkâr eder

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r5.claim: Even if God did nothing else for people, His ownership of the life He granted would require faith, worship, and not forgetting Him in attachment to life.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r5.anchor: Allah size hiçbir şey yapmamış ve yapmayacak olsa bile hayatınızın mâliki olduğu için sizin O’na iman ve ubûdiyet etmeniz

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r6.claim: Elmalılı voices the objection that inevitable death may seem to justify clinging passionately to temporary pleasures, despite its devastation of homes, families, and lives, then calls that a wretched error.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r6.anchor: Mâdem ki öleceğiz ve mâdem ki Allah verdiğini alıyor, o hâlde hayat elimize geçmiş iken iyi kötü mümkin olan ne zevki varsa görelim diyoruz

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r7.claim: Even on that mistaken premise, people should seek enjoyment lawfully, treat gratitude and sincerity to God as the greatest pleasure, and love and fear Him for their broad benefits in this life.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r7.anchor: hayatın bu zevklerini böyle körü körüne ve çılgıncasına değil, tarîk-i meşrû‘ile istîfâya çalışmak ve Allah teâlâ’ya ihlâs ve şükrânı en büyük bir zevk bilmek

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r8.claim: God will revive people after death and grant another life, at least as excellent as the first; resurrection after death is true.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r8.anchor: O sizi öldürdükten sonra yine diriltir ve diriltecektir. Size evvel verdiği gibi ve hatta ondan daha a‘lâ yine bir hayat verir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r9.claim: The repeatability visible throughout the universe underlies natural laws, knowledge, and craft: people can plant seeds, cultivate fields, harvest crops, and repeatedly build or use vehicles because things recur.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r9.anchor: Eğer olmasa idi sen kâinatta hiçbir kanun göremezdin, bir yaptığını bir daha yapamazdın, ilimden, sanattan hiçbir hissen olmazdı

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r10.claim: Humans cannot yet produce and restore life because they do not know life’s law or the primordial secrets of matter and spirits, and lack the power to create in its essence.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r10.anchor: henüz kānûn-ı hayâtı bilemediğinden, henüz maddelerin, rûhların esrâr-ı evveliyesine nüfuz edemediğinden, daha esasında yaratmak, halk etmek kudretine bizzat mâlik olamadığındandır

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r11.claim: People cannot see original matter or force, only their products, and their knowledge and power correspond to those manifestations; discovering matter’s secrets would not reveal every force, spirit, or angel or confer creative power.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r11.anchor: Sen asl-ı maddeyi, kuvveti göremezsin, gördüğün onların hâsılları, tezahürleridir. İlmin, fehmin, kudretin de bunlarla mütenâsibdir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r12.claim: People can only use matter and force as given; through a more particular relation to God they may, by His permission, gain insight into the mystery of life and reviving.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r12.anchor: onları olduğu kadar alıp Hak teâlâ’nın verdiği rûhunla tasarruf edebileceksin ve bizzat Hak teâlâ’ya daha husûsî bir nisbet peyda edebilirsen

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r13.claim: Inability to understand or create life does not justify denying the life and life-law already present and applied in each person; these necessarily point to a supreme being who makes and knows them.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r13.anchor: ortada mevcud olan hayat ve ihyâyı da inkâr edemezsin ya? Nefsü’l-emrde bir hayatın ve bir hayat kanununun cereyânında şüphe edemezsin

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r14.claim: Since God made and knows life and its law, what died will live again, and only God can accomplish it; He alone knows how and where, while revelation assures its occurrence.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r14.anchor: bu hayatı yapan ve bunun kanununu bilen bir zât-ı a‘lâ vardır. Hayat ve kānûn-ı hayat hak ve onu yapan ve bilen Hak teâlâ’dır

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r15.claim: The next life may occur on earth, in heaven, in the grave, or at the Resurrection; its conditions exceed present human understanding, and the afterlife is preceded by the interval of barzakh and grave life.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r15.anchor: Dilerse yerde yapar, dilerse göğe çıkarır, dilerse kabirde yapar, dilerse kıyamette; her hâlde bu bizim diğer bir şe’nimiz

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r16.claim: Elmalılı reports two readings of the revival: life in the grave or the resurrection after the Day of Judgment; either way, events continue beyond this life.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r16.anchor: Buradaki ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ hayat-ı kabir ile de tefsir edilmiştir. Kıyametten sonra neşr ile de tefsir edilmiştir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r17.claim: People return to God and are judged by the qualities acquired in their first life, passing the balance to receive reward or punishment; the truth of this is expressed in 99:7–8.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r17.anchor: bu ilk hayatta ne haslet iktisab ettinizse ona göre mîzandan geçecek, mükâfat ve mücâzâtına ereceksiniz

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r18.claim: At that time, the people of Paradise and divine approval will say, “Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.”
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r18.anchor: Ve o zaman ehl-i cennet ve rıdvân اَلْحَمْدُ للهِّ رَبِّ الْعَالَم۪ينَ diyeceklerdir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r19.claim: Elmalılı prays that God help everyone pass the stages of the grave and hereafter with ease and grant them complete faith, righteous deeds, and a good end.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#2/r19.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak cümlemize imdad etsin, bu geçitleri suhûletle, tatlılıkla geçirsin, îmân-ı kâmil, amel-i sâlih ile hüsn-i hâtime nasib etsin

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r12.claim: The passage summarizes humanity's pre-life nonexistence, expands the earlier description of earth and heaven as habitation, proves God's lordship, and summons deniers to gratitude and worship.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r12.anchor: nihâyet inâyet ve rahmet-i ilâhiyenin vüs‘ati ile zât ve sıfât-ı ilâhiyeyi münkirlere isbat

ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r7.claim: People should recall these gifts, investigate what was prepared for their benefit, use it in God's way, prepare for the afterlife, and aspire upward because they will return to God.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r7.anchor: bu edvârı, bu nimetleri derhâtır ediniz, rûhunuzun ne gibi ulviyetlere namzet kılındığını düşününüz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r1.claim: Signs throughout the human body and the nearby and distant cosmos show God's existence and unity; human creation, life, and death are among them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r1.anchor: İnsanın kendi vücudunda, yakın ve uzak çevresinde (kâinatta) Allah’ın varlığını ve birliğini gösteren sayısız işaret ve delil vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r2.claim: People infer an agent when a stone moves or a plant grows; the far greater intricacy and order of human life points all the more strongly to a maker.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r2.anchor: İnsanın hayatı ve yapısı, bir taşın hareketi ve bir otun bitmesiyle kıyas edilemeyecek kadar karmaşık, büyük, ince, sanatlı, düzenli, hesaplı ve esrarlıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r3.claim: Failing to reach God by reflecting on people and life would require a sealed heart or an intellect veiled and conditioned by the ego, Satan, or bad education.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r3.anchor: İnsanı ve hayatı düşünüp de Allah’a ulaşmamak için insanın kalbinin mühürlenmiş, aklının nefis, şeytan, yanlış eğitim yüzünden perdelenmiş ve şartlanmış olması gerekir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r4.claim: Birth and death are observable; the prophets taught resurrection after death, accountability for worldly deeds, and treatment according to the outcome of that reckoning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r4.anchor: Allah’ın peygamberleri, insanın öldükten sonra tekrar dirileceğini, dünyada yapıp ettiklerinin hesabını vereceğini, hesabın sonucuna göre muamele göreceğini haber vermişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r5.claim: Unconditioned natural reason can accept resurrection: by analogy, giving life again after death is easier for the One who created and gave life from nothing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r5.anchor: Tam aksine akıl, yok iken yaratıp hayat verenin öldürdükten sonra yeniden hayat vermesinin daha kolay olacağını kıyas metodu ile kolayca çıkarır ve kabullenir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r6.claim: The opening describes humans as lifeless or literally dead before being given life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r6.anchor: Burada insanlara “cansız nesneler” iken (lafzî anlamıyla “ölüler” iken) hayat verildiği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r7.speaker: bazı kimseler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r7.claim: Some inferred that there must have been a life before the initial state of being dead, and from this arose belief in repeated deaths and rebirths in other bodies.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r7.anchor: Baştaki “ölüler iken diriltilme” ifadesi bazı kimselerin aklına, ilk ölü olma halinden önce de bir hayatın bulunması gerektiği düşüncesini getirmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r8.claim: The Qur'an and hadith cannot support or prove reincarnation; repeated embodiment is not a valid reading of the verse.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r8.anchor: Bu inancı, Kur’an-ı Kerîm ve hadislerden çıkartmak ve delillendirmek mümkün değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r9.claim: Applying the principle that Qur'anic verses explain one another, the author rejects reading this verse as repeated deaths followed by rebirth in a different body each time.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r9.anchor: “Kur’an âyetleri birbirini açıklar” kaidesinden hareket ederek 28. âyeti ele alırsak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r10.claim: Qur'an 40:11 says there are two deaths and two revivals, which the author uses to interpret the present verse.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r10.anchor: Mü’min sûresindeki meâli verilen âyete göre “Ölmek de iki keredir, dirilmek de iki keredir.”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r11.claim: The preferred reconciliation is that humans were nonexistent before birth, then created and given life, died once in earthly life, and were resurrected after the world's end for the afterlife: two deaths and two revivals overall.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r11.anchor: İnsanlar yaratılmadan, doğmadan önce yokturlar ve bu bakımdan ölü gibidirler. Önce bu ölülere, yani yok olanlara varlık ve hayat verilmiştir. Bu “birinci diriltme”dir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r12.speaker: Ebü’l-Muîn en-Nesefî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r12.claim: Another possible reading is that a living person dies at the appointed time, is revived in the grave, dies again after the first questioning, and is revived after the Resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r12.anchor: Yaşayan insan eceli gelince ölür, sonra kabirde diriltilir; ilk sorgudan sonra tekrar ölür ve kıyametten sonra tekrar diriltilir (Ebü’l-Muîn en-Nesefî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r13.claim: Calling creation from nonexistence a revival while dead is metaphorical, leaving the two actual deaths and revivals in the verse of al-Mu'min explained.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r13.anchor: Yok iken yaratılma ve can vermeye “ölü iken diriltme” demek mecazi olduğu için gerçek mânada iki kere ölme ve dirilme olayı da Mü’min sûresindeki âyette açıklanmış olmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r14.claim: Whatever interpretation of the death and revival verses one adopts, the count remains two of each and contradicts reincarnation; Islamic teachings on human purpose, worldly life, resurrection, recompense, and soul-discipline also rule it out.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r14.anchor: Ölmek ve dirilmekle ilgili âyetler nasıl yorumlanırsa yorumlansın, ölmenin iki ve dirilmenin de iki kereden ibaret olması sonucu değişmez.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r15.claim: Reincarnation has no rational or scientific evidence, and living people have no conscious knowledge of having lived previously in another body.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r15.anchor: Yeniden bedenlenmenin aklî ve ilmî bakımdan da hiçbir delili yoktur. Dünyada yaşayan 6 milyar insanın, daha önce gelip bir başka bedende yaşadıklarına dair bilgileri ve şuurları mevcut değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r16.claim: Past-life-like information given under hypnosis or suggestion must have other explanations; proposed theories include collective consciousness, dreamlike images, contact with jinn, and memory errors.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:28/r16.anchor: Nitekim kolektif şuur, rüya benzeri görüntüler, cinlerle temas, hâfızanın oyunları gibi nazariyelerle bu tür açıklamalar yapılmaktadır.

BURHAN:v4p330/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p330/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p330/r1.claim: كيف asks about a thing's state, unlike ما which asks about its nature and من which asks about an individual; it functions like an adverbial predicate meaning in what state.
BURHAN:v4p330/r1.anchor: استفهام عن حال الشيء لا عن ذاته كما إن ما سؤال عن حقيقته ومن عن مشخصاته

BURHAN:v4p330/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p330/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v4p330/r2.claim: كيف can be a direct question, describe a state without asking, or express astonishment; context can also give it other rhetorical forces.
BURHAN:v4p330/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم لها ثلاثة أوجه أحدها سؤال محض عن حال

BURHAN:v4p330/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p330/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURHAN:v4p330/r3.claim: Al-Raghib reads كيف here as an admonitory inquiry rather than a request for unknown information; God's uses of كيف remind or rebuke the audience.
BURHAN:v4p330/r3.anchor: قال الراغب فى تفسيره كيف هنا استخبار لا استفهام

BURHAN:v4p330/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p330/r4.speaker: غيره
BURHAN:v4p330/r4.claim: Another account gives كيف several contextual functions: denial, rebuke, warning, prompting reflection, and confirming what precedes it; its force of denial can be followed by إلا.
BURHAN:v4p330/r4.anchor: ولتضمنها معنى الجحد شاع إن يقع بعدها إلا

BURHAN:v2p315/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r1.speaker: قوم
BURHAN:v2p315/r1.claim: Some hold that Qur'anic meanings cannot be exhaustively classified; others leave them unclassified, as Ibn al-Sayyid reports of most Basrans in his time.
BURHAN:v2p315/r1.anchor: زعم قوم ان معاني القرآن لا تنحصر

BURHAN:v2p315/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p315/r2.claim: Speech is classified variously: as two kinds, or ten; other schemes reduce the count to nine, eight, or seven by subsuming question, intercession, or doubt under other categories.
BURHAN:v2p315/r2.anchor: وقيل تسعة واسقطوا الاستفهام لدخوله في المسالة

BURHAN:v2p315/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
BURHAN:v2p315/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash counts six speech functions: report, inquiry, command, prohibition, call, and wish.
BURHAN:v2p315/r3.anchor: وكان أبو الحسن الأخفش يرى أنها ستة أيضا وهي عنده الخبر والاستخبار والأمر والنهي والنداء والتمني

BURHAN:v2p315/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r4.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p315/r4.claim: A five-part scheme lists report, command, declaration, request, and call; other classifications also exist.
BURHAN:v2p315/r4.anchor: وقيل خمسة الخبر والأمر والتصريح والطلب والنداء وقيل غير ذلك

BURHAN:v2p315/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p315/r5.claim: A report aims to inform its audience but can carry secondary functions such as astonishment.
BURHAN:v2p315/r5.anchor: والقصد به إفادة المخاطب وقد يشرب مع ذلك معاني اخر

BURHAN:v2p315/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r6.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v2p315/r6.claim: Ibn Faris defines astonishment as recognizing a thing's superiority over its peers by some quality.
BURHAN:v2p315/r6.anchor: وهو تفضيل الشيء على أضرابه بوصف

BURHAN:v2p315/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r7.speaker: ابن الضائع
BURHAN:v2p315/r7.claim: Ibn al-Da'i describes astonishment as an outstanding quality that sets the object apart from its peers.
BURHAN:v2p315/r7.anchor: وقال ابن الضائع استعظام صفة خرج بها المتعجب منه عن نظائره

BURHAN:v2p315/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p315/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says astonishment magnifies an extraordinary matter in listeners' hearts because it exceeds its peers.
BURHAN:v2p315/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في تفسير سورة الصف

BURHAN:v2p315/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r9.speaker: الرماني
BURHAN:v2p315/r9.claim: Al-Rummani says astonishment works through ambiguity: people wonder at causes they do not know, and obscurity strengthens the effect.
BURHAN:v2p315/r9.anchor: وقال الرماني المطلوب فى التعجب الإبهام لأن من شأن الناس ان يتعجبوا

BURHAN:v2p315/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p315/r10.claim: Astonishment has explicit forms ما أفعله and أفعل به, and indirect forms such as كبر and كيف in this verse.
BURHAN:v2p315/r10.anchor: ثم قد وضعوا للتعجب صيغا من لفظه وهي ما افعله

BURHAN:v2p315/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p315/r11.speaker: الثمانيني
BURHAN:v2p315/r11.claim: Al-Thumani argues that astonishment forms are declarative: أسمع بهم وأبصر means how well they hear and see; God informs people that they merit others' astonishment.

BURHAN:v3p214/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p214/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p214/r4.claim: The circumstantial clause in 2:28 likewise means وقد كنتم أمواتا, with قد omitted.
BURHAN:v3p214/r4.anchor: لأن الماضي لا يقع موقع الحال إلا وقد معه ظاهرة أو مقدرة

BURHAN:v1p139/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p139/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p139/r1.claim: The concordance notes أمواتا in the accusative in Baqarah, Ali Imran, and al-Mursalat, alongside comparable formula and spelling variations across surahs.

BURHAN:v1p139/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p139/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p139/r3.claim: Other listed parallels include ونزلنا in three surahs versus وأنزلنا elsewhere, فإن توليتم in three, ألم يروا without waw in three, and specified forms of أجل, تراب, and إرسال الرسل.
BURHAN:v1p139/r3.anchor: ﴿ ونزلنا ﴾ ثلاثة أحرف فى طه والنحل وق

ITQAN:v2p496#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p496#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p496#3/r1.claim: كيف is either conditional, as in several verses, with its answer omitted when the preceding context makes it clear, or—more commonly—interrogative.
ITQAN:v2p496#3/r1.anchor: وجوابها في ذلك كله محذوف لدلالة ما قبلها

ITQAN:v2p496#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p496#3/r2.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p496#3/r2.claim: Al-Raghib says interrogative كيف asks about a thing's state, not its essence, and concerns what can be called similar or dissimilar; therefore one cannot ask “how” of God.
ITQAN:v2p496#3/r2.anchor: قال الراغب وإنما يسأل بها عما يصح أن يقال فيه شبيه وغير شبيه ولهذا لا يصح أن يقال في الله كيف

ITQAN:v2p496#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p496#3/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p496#3/r3.claim: When God uses كيف, it is a question that alerts or rebukes the addressee, as in “How can you disbelieve?”
ITQAN:v2p496#3/r3.anchor: لا يصح أن يقال في الله كيف قال وكلما أخبر الله بلفظ كيف عن نفسه فهو استخبار

ITQAN:v3p205/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p205/r1.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v3p205/r1.claim: Ibn Faris defines astonishment as distinguishing a thing from its counterparts.
ITQAN:v3p205/r1.anchor: قال ابن فارس وهو تفصيل شيء على أضرابه

ITQAN:v3p205/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p205/r2.speaker: ابن الصائغ
ITQAN:v3p205/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sa'igh defines astonishment as deeming a quality so exceptional that its subject exceeds comparable things.
ITQAN:v3p205/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الصائغ استعظام صفة خرج بها المتعجب منه عن نظائره

ITQAN:v3p205/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p205/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v3p205/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says astonishment magnifies an event in listeners' hearts, since people marvel at what departs from its peers.
ITQAN:v3p205/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري معنى التعجب تعظيم الأمر في قلوب السامعين لأن التعجب لا يكون إلا من شيء خارج عن نظائره وأشكاله

ITQAN:v3p205/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p205/r4.speaker: الرماني
ITQAN:v3p205/r4.claim: Al-Rummani says astonishment aims at making the cause unclear; the more obscure the cause, the stronger the astonishment, whose original subject is a matter with a hidden cause.
ITQAN:v3p205/r4.anchor: وقال الرماني المطلوب في التعجب الإبهام لأن من شأن الناس أن يتعجبوا مما لا يعرف سببه فكلما استبهم السبب كان التعجب أحسن

ITQAN:v3p205/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p205/r5.speaker: الرماني
ITQAN:v3p205/r5.claim: Al-Rummani calls the form an astonishment expression figuratively; he says نعم takes a generic noun to magnify it before the later explanation.
ITQAN:v3p205/r5.anchor: وأصل التعجب إنما هو للمعنى الخفي سببه والصيغة الدالة عليه تسمى تعجبا مجازا

ITQAN:v3p205/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p205/r6.speaker: الرماني
ITQAN:v3p205/r6.claim: Al-Rummani connects نعم's restriction to a genus with magnification, followed by an explanatory specification.
ITQAN:v3p205/r6.anchor: إلا في الجنس من أجل التفخيم ليقع التفسير على نحو التفخيم

ITQAN:v3p205/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p205/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p205/r7.claim: Astonishment has dedicated forms ما أفعل and أفعل به, and other forms such as كبر and كيف تكفرون بالله; كبرت and كبر مقتا are examples.
ITQAN:v3p205/r7.anchor: ثم قد وضعوا للتعجب صيغاً من لفظه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r1.claim: Life ordinarily denotes animate beings’ sensation and movement; figurative uses depend on contextual clues.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r1.anchor: الحياة : معنى يفيد الحيوان الحس والتحرك ، وتستعار الحياة في مواضع تدل عليها القرينة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r2.claim: The first sense of life is the initial creation of living beings: sperm drops into which God breathed spirit.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r2.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحياة في القرآن على خمسة أوجه : - أحدها : نفخ الروح في الحيوان بالخلق الأول

BURHAN:v3p354/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.claim: The four broken plural forms of paucity and the two sound plurals are inherently paucity forms; other plurals may indicate few or many as context determines, as Qur'anic examples show.
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.anchor: واعلم أن جموع التكثير الأربعة وجمعى التصحيح أعنى جمع التأنيث وجمع التذكير كل ذلك للقلة

BURHAN:v3p242/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p242/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p242/r6.claim: Several explanations account for mentioning death before life: the order subdues creatures, human life is like death and leads back to death, and life follows death.
BURHAN:v3p242/r6.anchor: منها أن فيه قهرا للخلق والمقام

BURHAN:v3p242/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p242/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p242/r7.claim: If death means nonexistence, it preceded life because humans were dead before receiving the spirit, as “you were dead, then He gave you life” indicates.
BURHAN:v3p242/r7.anchor: ومنها أن الموت تقدم في الوجود إذ الإنسان قبل نفخ الروح فيه كان ميتا لعدم الروح

BURHAN:v2p342/r15.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p342/r15.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p342/r15.claim: The sixteenth use is wonder, illustrated by Solomon wondering where the hoopoe is and by How can you disbelieve in God?
BURHAN:v2p342/r15.anchor: السادس عشر التعجب نحو ﴿ ما لي لا أرى الهدهد ﴾ 1 ﴿ كيف تكفرون بالله ﴾ 2

BURHAN:v2p342/r16.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p342/r16.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v2p342/r16.claim: Some classify كيف تكفرون بالله as an alert rather than wonder.

BURHAN:v4p332/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p332/r4.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v4p332/r4.claim: Sibawayh treats كيف in كيف تكفرون as adverbial, “in what state”; al-Akhfash instead parses it as a circumstantial expression, “in what state are you disbelieving?”
BURHAN:v4p332/r4.anchor: وعلى الحال عند الأخفش أي على حال تكفرون

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r4.claim: Kāna can be a connective or extra element in formulations of God’s attributes.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r4.anchor: والثاني : أن تكون صلة . ومنه قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r4.claim: Mawt can mean the semen stage; the first of two deaths is being a drop before life.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r4.anchor: والثاني : النطفة . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f10.claim: The first revival follows the original lifeless state without delay, so it takes fa; death and the second revival occur later, so they take thumma.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f10.anchor: لأن الإحياء الأول قد تعقب الموت بغير تراخي وأما الموت فقد تراخى عن الإحياء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p633/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p633/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p633/r2.claim: With ḍamma, thumma is a conjunction marking order with delay, as in 2:28 and 18:37; with fatḥa, thamma is an adverb meaning “there,” as in 26:64.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p633/r2.anchor: ثُمّ بضمّ الثاء هي حرف عطف تفيد الترتيب والتراخي

NASHR:v2p236/r28.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r28.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p236/r28.claim: Yaʿqūb affirms the yāʾs in فارهبون, فاتقون, and تكفرون both at pause and in continuation.
NASHR:v2p236/r28.anchor: فارهبون، فاتقون. تكفرون أثبتهن في الحالتين يعقوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r1.claim: The address returns to the people commanded in 2:21 after the intervening clauses from 2:25 through 2:27 have run their course.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r1.anchor: ثني عنان الخطاب إلى الناس الذين خوطبوا بقوله آنفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r2.claim: The turn is not an iltifāt from 2:26's report of disbelievers' words, since this verse is not locally connected to that passage; the link is shared purpose after an interruption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r2.anchor: تناسب مع قوله : { إن الله لا يستحي أن يضرب مثلا ما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.claim: The reasons for worship in 2:21–22 are paired with reasons against disbelief here: creation and provision are followed by life, death, resurrection, return, and creation of what is on earth, preparing for the account of human origins and stages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.anchor: ومن بديع المناسبة وفائق التفنن في ضروب الانتقالات في المخاطبات أن كانت العلل التي قرن بها الأمر بعبادة الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r4.claim: The people addressed by takfurūn are the polytheists, since Jews did not disbelieve in God or deny the second resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r4.anchor: متعين رجوعه إلى ( الناس ) وهم المشركون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r5.claim: Kayfa is an interrogative noun of state, semantically vague but still nominal and therefore declinable; it most often asks about a general condition and is parsed as a circumstantial adverb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r5.anchor: اسم لا يعرف اشتقاقه يدل على حالة خاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r6.claim: The question expresses astonishment and denunciation: in light of the states that follow, disbelief should be unacceptable to sound judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r6.anchor: والاستفهام هنا مستعمل في التعجيب والإنكار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r7.claim: The rhetorical question demands a reason that could excuse disbelief; if the addressees offer none, the failure itself warrants blame and threat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r7.anchor: وكأن المنكر يريد أن يقطع معذرة المخاطب فيظهر له أنه يتطلب منه الجواب بما يظهر السبب

DAMGHANI:v1p148/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p148/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p148/r11.claim: Aḥyā can mean the initial creation of people who had not existed before.
DAMGHANI:v1p148/r11.anchor: فوجه منها : الحياة يعني الخلق الأول وذلك قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة
